description:
NanomediGene is developing a precision nanoparticle delivery platform designed to rescue clinically tested cancer targets that were limited by systemic toxicity.

Our lead program focuses on triple-negative breast cancer, using a TROP2-targeted PLGA nanoparticle approach to deliver PF-05175157, a dual ACC1/ACC2 inhibitor originally tested by Pfizer. title: INAVO120: What the Abstract Didn't Tell You About the Control Arm | The Source Report #breastcancer
description:
INAVO120 OS update was published in the NEJM. Inavolisib plus palbociclib-fulvestrant improves OS by 7 months in PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- breast cancer. HR 0.67.

But the abstract does not mention what happened to the control arm after progression.

These are PIK3CA-mutated patients. Alpelisib has been FDA-approved for this population since 2019. Only 10% of control arm patients who received second-line therapy got a PI3K inhibitor. The post-progression therapy does not reflect the US standard of care.

The OS benefit is real. But interpret those 7 months knowing that one may argue that the control arm was undertreated by US standards. 

This appraisal was produced using The Source Report, a structured AI-assisted critical appraisal methodology under physician oversight. Full methodology and counter abstract on Substack: https://allenlimd.substack.com/p/inavo120-achieves-the-os-that-solar

title: Does a lower cancer drug dose mean worse treatment? #lungcancer #lungcancertreatment
description:
If your doctor reduces your cancer drug dose, it can feel like bad news.
It isn't.

→ What a dose reduction actually means:

It's not a sign the treatment has stopped working. It doesn't mean you're getting less of what you need.

It means your doctor is personalising the dose for your body.

→ The goal was never the highest dose:

The right dose isn't written in a trial protocol. It's the dose your body can tolerate while still controlling the cancer.

And that number is different for everyone.

→ A real example:

For lorlatinib, a targeted treatment for a specific type of lung cancer with an ALK mutation, 75mg works just as well as 100mg for most people.

So dropping to that dose doesn't reduce the chance of success. It just gets the balance right for you.

→ Why it matters beyond the numbers:

When side effects are managed, everything else improves too.
You stay active. You eat properly. You get on with your life.

And that isn't just quality of life. It can improve your survival too.
The goal is never the highest dose you can tolerate.

It's the best dose that gives you the best life, with the best treatment outcome.

title: Clinical Trial Representation in the Genomic Era: Challenges and Solutions
description:
The full article for this interview is available on Oncology Data Advisor. Check it out here:
https://oncdata.com/clinical-trial-representation-cha-friedson

As cancer treatments become more targeted in the era of precision medicine, traditional methods for measuring clinical trial representation are falling behind. In this interview, June Cha, PhD, and Andrew Friedson, PhD, discuss their recent report, Measuring Representation in Clinical Trials: Simulations Demonstrating How Current Methods Fail in the Context of Precision Medicine.

Dr. Cha and Dr. Friedson explore the limitations of current methodologies, which often rely on broad cancer registries that fail to capture the genetic and molecular nuances of specific subpopulations. They highlight the need for more granular registry data, AI-driven cohort building, and federal collaboration to improve trial accuracy and ensure real-world efficacy.

For oncologists, the conversation emphasizes the importance of scrutinizing trial data for external validity, asking critical questions about comparator groups, and ensuring that trial populations align with the specific biomarkers and demographics of their patients.

नई दवाएं: कुछ आधुनिक कीमोथेरेपी दवाएं इतनी आक्रामक तरीके से स्वस्थ कोशिकाओं पर हमला नहीं करतीं, जिससे बालों की जड़ें सुरक्षित रहती हैं।

क्योंकि बालों के रोम की कोशिकाओं में वे विशिष्ट "Targets" नहीं होते, इसलिए वे दवा की मार से बच जाते हैं।

title: Discovery of a Small Molecule HPK1 Inhibitor for Immuno-Oncology
description:
HPK1 (hematopoietic progenitor kinase 1, MAP4K1) is a negative regulator of T-cell signaling and has emerged as a promising new target in immuno-oncology. Inhibition of HPK1 is expected to enhance immune system activation and promote T-cell-mediated tumor cell killing. However, achieving sufficient kinase selectivity presents a major challenge, as inhibition of anti-target kinases involved in productive T cell signaling could lead to undesired immunosuppression.

In this Flash Talk, Rebecca Gallego, Associate Research Fellow at Pfizer, will present the discovery and optimization of a potent and selective HPK1 inhibitor. She will discuss how mechanistic cellular assays were used to quantify HPK1 inhibition, alongside functional assays and biochemical profiling to evaluate kinase selectivity and avoid key anti-targets. This presentation will highlight how lipophilic efficiency analysis and structure-based drug design guided optimization efforts ultimately led to the discovery of PF-07265028, a potent and selective HPK1 inhibitor which advanced to a Phase 1 clinical trial.

  * **Caution with Supplements**: Not all supplements are helpful, and certain medications like unnecessary antibiotics can disrupt your balance.

title: ब्रेस्ट कैंसर में PET CT करना क्यों जरूरी है? #petct#education #cancerawareness #cancermyths #cancer
description:
ब्रेस्ट कैंसर (Breast Cancer) के इलाज और मैनेजमेंट में PET-CT स्कैन एक महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। इसे सामान्यतः तब करवाया जाता है जब डॉक्टर को यह पता लगाना होता है कि कैंसर शरीर के अन्य हिस्सों में फैला है या नहीं।

यहाँ कुछ प्रमुख कारण दिए गए हैं कि ब्रेस्ट कैंसर में इसकी आवश्यकता क्यों होती है।

1. कैंसर के स्टेज का सटीक निर्धारण (Staging)

PET-CT स्कैन यह देखने के लिए सबसे प्रभावी है कि क्या कैंसर ब्रेस्ट और बगल की गांठों (Lymph nodes) से निकलकर शरीर के अन्य अंगों जैसे कि हड्डियों, लीवर, फेफड़ों या मस्तिष्क तक तो नहीं पहुँच गया है। इसे 'मेटास्टेसिस' (Metastasis) की जाँच करना कहते हैं।

2. इलाज के असर की जाँच (Monitoring Treatment)

कीमोथेरेपी या अन्य उपचार शुरू करने के बाद, यह स्कैन डॉक्टर को यह समझने में मदद करता है कि ट्यूमर दवाओं पर कैसी प्रतिक्रिया दे रहा है। यदि कैंसर कोशिकाएं कम सक्रिय हो रही हैं, तो PET स्कैन में उनकी चमक (Tracer uptake) कम हो जाती है।

3. सर्जरी से पहले की योजना

यदि कैंसर का आकार बड़ा है या वह जटिल स्थिति में है, तो सर्जन यह सुनिश्चित करना चाहते हैं कि सर्जरी के बाद कैंसर का कोई भी हिस्सा शरीर के दूसरे हिस्से में सक्रिय न रह जाए।

4. कैंसर की वापसी का पता लगाना (Recurrence)

इलाज पूरा होने के कुछ समय बाद अगर डॉक्टर को शक हो कि कैंसर वापस आ गया है, तो PET-CT स्कैन शरीर के किसी भी हिस्से में छिपी हुई कैंसर कोशिकाओं को पकड़ने में मदद करता है।

title: Most patients walk into their first immunotherapy appointment focused on the infusion itself.
description:
Most patients walk into their first immunotherapy appointment focused on the infusion itself. 
 
But a few conversations before treatment starts can make the experience safer and less stressful 💜
 
🌸 Review your medication list with your team. That includes recent antibiotics and acid suppressing medications. Some studies have linked these with worse immunotherapy outcomes, but the data are still emerging. Do not stop anything on your own. Just make sure your team knows.
 
🌺 Build the strongest nutrition foundation you can. A balanced, fibre rich diet from beans, vegetables, fruit, and whole grains is a good goal. Research connecting diet and immunotherapy response is growing but still evolving.
 
🌸 Check whether your vaccines are up to date. Ideally this is reviewed before treatment begins. Timing should be individualised with your oncology team.
 
🌺 Ask what food precautions actually apply to you. In general, avoid raw or undercooked meat, seafood, and eggs, and wash produce well under running water.
 
🌸 Take care of logistics before day one. Transportation, meals, prescriptions, and who to call if side effects show up. A plan lowers stress even when treatment goes smoothly.

title: Could COPD make immunotherapy work better for lung cancer patients? #lungcancertreatment #lungcancer
description:
Could COPD actually make immunotherapy work better?

It sounds counterintuitive. But there's emerging evidence that the inflammation caused by COPD might be doing something useful.

→ What's happening in the lungs:

COPD changes the immune environment around a tumour. Certain immune cells, including T cells that help fight cancer, expand in the inflamed tissue surrounding it.

That's exactly what immunotherapy is designed to trigger. In some people with COPD, it may already be happening.

→ What this means in practice:

The inflammation in your lungs isn't necessarily working against you. It may be priming your immune system in the right place to fight the cancer, and immunotherapy could build on that.

→ What we don't know yet:

This is one piece of a much larger puzzle. Every person's immune system responds differently. Response rates aren't guaranteed to be higher in COPD, and the science is still emerging.

But it offers genuine encouragement and helps explain why two people on the same treatment can have completely different outcomes.

→ A question worth asking your oncologist:

"What is it about my case that makes you think I'm more likely to respond to this treatment rather than another one?"

Your response to treatment isn't about what happened to the average person in the study. It's about what's going to happen to you.

description:
“Chemotherapy" — yeh ek word hi kaafi hai logon ko darr jaane ke liye. But what if everything you feared about it was only half the truth?

📌 ABOUT THIS VIDEO 
In this episode, Dr. Belal Bin Asaf breaks down one of the most
misunderstood parts of lung cancer treatment — chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. Most patients associate chemotherapy with hair loss and vomiting and refuse it out of fear. But today's cancer treatment has gone far beyond traditional chemo. Targeted therapy works like a laser-guided missile — hitting only cancer cells without damaging healthy ones. Immunotherapy trains your own immune system to recognize and destroy cancer cells. And both are decided not by one doctor, but by a multidisciplinary tumor board. If you've been avoiding treatment because of fear — this episode will change your mind.

🔴 3 THINGS IN THIS VIDEO THAT WILL CHANGE HOW YOU SEE CHEMOTHERAPY:

🔴 The side effects of chemotherapy — hair loss, vomiting — are temporary and resolve once treatment ends. Fear of side effects should never be a reason to avoid life-saving treatment.

title: Immunization/vaccination #viral #shorts #trending #nursing #education #science #youtubeshorts
description:
1. Definition
Immunization is the process by which a person becomes protected against a disease through the administration of a vaccine. It helps the immune system recognize and fight harmful microorganisms such as bacteria and viruses.

2. Types of Immunization
A. Active Immunization
Involves giving a vaccine that stimulates the body’s immune system.

The body produces its own antibodies.

Protection develops slowly but lasts long.

Examples:

BCG vaccine (for tuberculosis)

Measles vaccine

Polio vaccine

B. Passive Immunization
Involves giving pre-formed antibodies.

Provides immediate protection.

Short-term effect.

Examples:

Tetanus immunoglobulin

Rabies immunoglobulin

3. Types of Vaccines
Live attenuated vaccines

Contain weakened organisms

Example: Measles, BCG

Inactivated (killed) vaccines

Contain dead organisms

Example: Polio (IPV), Rabies

Subunit / Recombinant vaccines

Contain parts of pathogens

Example: Hepatitis B

Toxoid vaccines

Contain inactivated toxins

Example: Tetanus toxoid

mRNA vaccines

Use genetic material to produce immune response

Example: COVID-19 vaccines

4. Immunization Schedule (India – Basic)
At birth: BCG, OPV, Hepatitis B

6, 10, 14 weeks: DPT, OPV, Hep B, Hib

9 months: Measles / MR

16–24 months: Booster doses

5 years: DPT booster

10 & 16 years: TT or Td

5. Importance of Immunization
Prevents infectious diseases

Reduces child mortality

Controls outbreaks

Provides herd immunity (protects community)

Cost-effective public health measure

6. Side Effects of Vaccines
Common (mild):

Fever

Pain or swelling at injection site

Rare (serious):

Allergic reactions

Anaphylaxis (very rare)

7. Contraindications
Severe allergic reaction to previous dose

Immunocompromised (for live vaccines)

Acute severe illness

8. Cold Chain (Vaccine Storage)
Vaccines must be stored at 2°C to 8°C

Maintains vaccine potency

Includes refrigerators, cold boxes, ice packs

9. Herd Immunity
When a large portion of the population is immunized, it reduces disease spread and protects unvaccinated individuals.

THE BRIEFING ON RNA - STUDY GUIDE

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
DNA is biology's most overrated molecule. It sits in the nucleus doing nothing while RNA copies, carries, builds, regulates, and then disintegrates. The molecule that runs every living cell has the structural permanence of a sneeze. Katalin Kariko spent decades being demoted and rejected trying to turn synthetic mRNA into medicine. Then a pandemic arrived, and the technology nobody would fund saved the world in two days of design and ten months of paperwork.

KEY CONCEPTS

The Central Dogma Deception
- Francis Crick named it in 1957: DNA makes RNA makes protein
- Presented as a one-way street with RNA as mere messenger
- Reality: RNA runs the post office, designs the routes, and builds the sorting machines
- The ribosome that constructs every protein is made mostly of RNA
- RNA accepted a demotion to "messenger" that lasted three billion years

The RNA World
- Before DNA, before proteins, RNA existed alone
- Stored genetic information AND catalyzed chemical reactions
- Both blueprint and bricklayer simultaneously
- The origin of life was probably RNA doing everything by itself
- Ribozymes prove RNA can be both information and enzyme

The Arithmetic Cheat
- Human genome: 20,000 genes
- Human body: over 100,000 proteins
- RNA alternative splicing creates multiple proteins from single genes
- DSCAM gene in fruit flies: 38,016 different proteins from ONE gene
- This is how biology cheats at math

Dark Matter RNA
- Only 2% of the genome codes for proteins
- The other 98% produces RNA with unknown functions
- We sequenced the entire human genome and declared victory
- Then discovered we read the book but not the language
- In 2020, we started writing new instructions we do not fully understand

KATALIN KARIKO TIMELINE

1995 - Demoted at University of Pennsylvania
1997 - Met Drew Weissman at a photocopier
2005 - Published pseudouridine breakthrough (not in Nature)
2005-2020 - Almost nobody cared
2020 - COVID pandemic made everyone care
2023 - Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine

THE PSEUDOURIDINE BREAKTHROUGH
- Lab-made mRNA was rejected by immune system like a fake ID
- Kariko and Weissman discovered swapping uridine for pseudouridine
- This single chemical letter substitution made synthetic mRNA invisible
- The paper was rejected by Nature and Science
- Published in a lesser journal, ignored for 15 years

COVID VACCINE TIMELINE

January 11, 2020 - China released virus genetic sequence
January 13, 2020 - Moderna finalized vaccine design (2 DAYS)
March 16, 2020 - First volunteer received injection (66 days)
December 2020 - FDA emergency authorization (10 months total)

The science took a weekend. The paperwork took the rest of the year.

VACCINE LOGISTICS
- mRNA degrades in minutes at room temperature
- Pfizer vaccine: minus 70 Celsius storage (colder than Mars)
- Moderna vaccine: minus 20 Celsius storage
- 13 billion doses administered worldwide

FUTURE APPLICATIONS
- 99+ clinical trials for mRNA cancer vaccines (as of late 2024)
- Process: sequence patient tumor, build custom instructions
- Wrap mRNA in lipid nanoparticles (tiny fat bubbles)
- Inject personalized cancer treatment
- The same technology that was rejected is now fighting cancer

STATISTICS THAT MATTER
- 4 billion years: how long RNA has been doing the work
- 2 days: vaccine design time
- 66 days: sequence to first injection
- 15 years: how long the breakthrough was ignored
- 13 billion: vaccine doses administered
- 98%: genome that produces unexplained RNA
- 38,016: proteins from one fruit fly gene

THE INSTITUTIONAL FAILURE
- Penn would not give Kariko tenure
- Nature would not publish the paper
- Science would not publish the paper
- NIH would not fund the research
- All of them were wrong

title: RNA Explained: Hiding in Plain Sight – RNA Modifications Enable Effective mRNA Vaccines
description:
How did a tiny chemical change to RNA revolutionize modern medicine? For decades, scientists dreamed of using messenger RNA (mRNA) to treat diseases. The potential was enormous. However, there was a hurdle for certain applications: our immune system.

When foreign mRNA enters a cell, it is usually recognized as a threat, triggering an immune response that blocks its function or destroys it entirely. It was discovered that subtle chemical modifications to the RNA building blocks—specifically replacing the base uridine with N1-methylpseudouridine—allowed the mRNA to slip past the cell's sensors undetected.

This "stealth" technology was important to developing effective COVID-19 vaccines in record time, and it is now being harnessed to create new therapies for cancer, infectious diseases, and rare genetic disorders.

This video is part of an eight-part series on RNA-related Nobel Prizes, serving as the final public outreach activity of the NCCR RNA & Disease. We are proud to share this project as we conclude our 12 years of operations at the end of April 2026.

title: Lula lê falas de Bolsonaro sobre vacinas e chama Eduardo Bolsonaro de “fujão”
description:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) voltou a criticar, nesta segunda-feira (11), a condução da pandemia da Covid-19 pelo governo do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL). Durante cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto em memória das vítimas da doença, Lula leu falas atribuídas a Bolsonaro em dezembro de 2020 sobre a compra de vacinas e afirmou que o então presidente insinuava supostos interesses financeiros na aquisição dos imunizantes.

No discurso, Lula também classificou o ex-deputado federal Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP) como “fujão que está nos Estados Unidos tentando pregar golpe contra o Brasil”. A fala ocorreu durante a cerimônia de sanção da lei que institui o Dia Nacional em Memória das Vítimas da Covid-19.

Ao relembrar o período mais crítico da pandemia, Lula citou o colapso enfrentado por Manaus, quando a rede de saúde viveu uma grave crise por falta de oxigênio hospitalar. O presidente afirmou que, após as declarações de Bolsonaro sobre vacinas, mais de 500 mil brasileiros ainda morreram em decorrência da doença.

A cerimônia marcou a sanção da lei que cria o Dia Nacional em Memória das Vítimas da Covid-19, celebrado em 12 de março, data associada ao registro da primeira morte pela doença no Brasil. A iniciativa busca preservar a memória das vítimas, acolher familiares e reforçar a importância da ciência, da vacinação e da preparação do país para futuras emergências sanitárias.

Durante o evento, Lula afirmou que o país precisa lembrar as falas e decisões tomadas durante a pandemia para evitar que erros semelhantes se repitam. O presidente também voltou a defender o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), a vacinação e a atuação de profissionais da saúde no enfrentamento à crise sanitária.

title: Lula critica desinformação sobre vacinas e cobra memória das vítimas da Covid-19
description:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) criticou, nesta segunda-feira (11), a disseminação de desinformação sobre vacinas durante a pandemia da Covid-19 no Brasil. A declaração foi feita durante cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto, em Brasília, na qual o governo sancionou a lei que institui o Dia Nacional em Memória das Vítimas da Covid-19.

Em seu discurso, Lula rechaçou falas que circularam durante a crise sanitária, como a de que pessoas imunizadas contra o coronavírus poderiam “virar jacaré” ou se tornar gays. O presidente afirmou que médicos, líderes religiosos e pessoas públicas ajudaram a espalhar informações falsas sobre a vacinação, o que, segundo ele, contribuiu para incentivar a ignorância em um momento de emergência nacional.

Lula também criticou ex-integrantes do governo de Jair Bolsonaro e defendeu que os responsáveis por propagar desinformação durante a pandemia sejam lembrados, para que episódios semelhantes não se repitam em futuras crises sanitárias. O presidente afirmou ainda esperar que “a justiça seja feita” em relação ao que ocorreu no período.

A cerimônia marcou a sanção da lei que estabelece o dia 12 de março como o Dia Nacional em Memória das Vítimas da Covid-19. A data faz referência ao registro da primeira morte pela doença no Brasil e tem como objetivo preservar a memória das vítimas, acolher familiares e reforçar a importância da ciência, da vacinação e das políticas públicas de saúde.

O Brasil registrou mais de 700 mil mortes pela Covid-19, em uma das maiores crises sanitárias da história do país. Durante o evento, representantes de associações de familiares das vítimas também defenderam a responsabilização de pessoas que ajudaram a espalhar desinformação sobre vacinas e tratamentos sem comprovação científica.

title: Sen. Ron Johnson Grills FDA Director On Memo Claiming COVID Vaccines Killed Children
description:
🚨 Sen. Ron Johnson grills FDA's top vaccine regulator over a memo claiming COVID-19 shots killed at least 10 children.

During a Senate hearing titled "The Corruption of Science and Federal Health Agencies," Sen. Johnson pressed Dr. Vinay Prasad — Director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research — on an internal memo he sent to staff. The memo stated that "at least 10 children have died after and because of receiving COVID-19 vaccination," based on an initial analysis of 96 deaths reported to VAERS between 2021 and 2024. The deaths were suggested to be linked to myocarditis, an inflammation of the heart muscle.

Sen. Johnson pressed Dr. Prasad on the lack of supporting detail in the memo. No data was shared on children's ages, pre-existing health conditions, or the methodology used to determine vaccine causation. A separate internal FDA memo from December 5 reportedly placed the pediatric death toll from COVID shots at somewhere between zero and seven — directly contradicting Prasad's figures. Twelve former FDA commissioners have also criticized Prasad's claims in the New England Journal of Medicine, arguing his proposals could "impede the ability to update vaccines" and pose "a threat to evidence-based vaccine policy."

The hearing comes as vaccine safety experts raise questions about the extraordinary nature of the claims and the absence of detailed data to support them. For context, CDC data shows approximately 2,000 children have died from COVID-19 itself, including 90 confirmed deaths between July 2024 and July 2025.

Recipes :-

1) Cinnamon tea
- Ingredients: 1-2 Cup water, 1 small stick Ceylon cinnamon or 1/2 tsp Ceylon cinnamon powder.
- Method: Boil water with the stick 5–10 min (or stir powdered cinnamon into hot water). Strain; drink warm.
- Serve: 1 cup daily.

2) Amla (Indian gooseberry) juice (quick, low-sugar)
- Ingredients: 2–3 fresh amla or 20–30 ml fresh unsweetened amla juice, 200–250 ml water.
- Method: Blend chopped amla with water, strain if desired. Dilute juice well; do not add sugar.
- Serve: Small glass (about 150–200 ml) once a day or alternate days.

3) Fenugreek seed water (soaked)
- Ingredients: 1 tsp fenugreek seeds, 250 ml water.
- Method: Soak seeds in water overnight. In the morning, strain and drink the soaking water; chew seeds if you like.
- Serve: Drink first thing in the morning (or spread intake across day).

4) Karela (bitter melon) powder drink (simple)
- Ingredients: 1/2 tsp karela powder, 200–250 ml water or unsweetened tomato/vegetable juice.
- Method: Mix powder into water/juice, stir and drink. Start with 1–2 times/week and increase if tolerated.
- Serve: Small glass; use sparingly because of bitter taste.

5) Lemon water (warm)
- Ingredients: 1 cup warm water, juice of 1/4–1/2 lemon.
- Method: Squeeze lemon into warm water; drink plain.
- Serve: Morning on empty stomach or before meals.

6) Golden milk with ashwagandha
- Ingredients (single cup): 200 ml unsweetened milk or unsweetened plant milk, 1/4 tsp turmeric, pinch black pepper, 1/4 tsp ashwagandha powder, optional 1/4 tsp cinnamon.
- Method: Warm milk, whisk in turmeric, black pepper, ashwagandha and cinnamon; simmer 2–3 minutes, strain if needed.
- Serve: 1 small cup—best in evening.

7) Green tea
- Ingredients: 1 green tea bag or 1 tsp loose leaves, 200–250 ml hot (not boiling) water.
- Method: Steep 2–3 minutes (longer = more caffeine/bitterness). Remove bag/strain and drink.
- Serve: 1–3 cups/day depending on caffeine tolerance.

8) Gudmar (Gymnema) tea
- Ingredients: 1 tsp dried gudmar leaves or 1–2 fresh leaves, 200–250 ml hot water.
- Method: Steep leaves 5–10 minutes, strain, drink warm.
- Serve: 1 cup once daily to start.

description:
O diabetes tipo 2 não é causado por um único problema.
É uma doença multifatorial — e é isso que o Octeto de DeFronzo explica.

Esse conceito mostra que existem 8 mecanismos principais alterados no diabetes tipo 2:

1️⃣ Pâncreas (células beta) → produz menos insulina
2️⃣ Pâncreas (células alfa) → excesso de glucagon
3️⃣ Fígado → libera glicose em excesso
4️⃣ Músculo → capta menos glicose
5️⃣ Tecido adiposo → aumenta liberação de gordura inflamatória
6️⃣ Intestino → redução do efeito incretina
7️⃣ Rim → reabsorve glicose demais
8️⃣ Cérebro → disfunção no controle da saciedade e metabolismo

👉 Ou seja: o diabetes não está só no açúcar.
Ele envolve vários órgãos trabalhando de forma desregulada.

💊 Como isso muda o tratamento?

Quando usamos medicamentos e hábitos que atacam múltiplos pontos do octeto, o controle melhora muito mais.

Exemplos:

• Metformina → reduz glicose do fígado
• SGLT2 (dapagliflozina) → age no rim
• GLP-1 / semaglutida → intestino, cérebro e pâncreas
• Exercício físico → melhora músculo
• Emagrecimento → melhora fígado, gordura visceral e resistência à insulina

📉 Quanto mais mecanismos você corrige, melhor a glicemia responde.

💡 É por isso que tratar diabetes tipo 2 hoje não é só “baixar açúcar”.

É corrigir o sistema inteiro.

Entender o octeto é entender por que dieta, exercício, perda de peso e medicações combinadas funcionam tão bem juntos.

title: Rosiglitazone: 42 trials, zero individual signals, one MA. #Shorts
description:
Rosiglitazone (Avandia) was the best-selling diabetes drug in the world by 2006. Each of its 42 individual regulatory trials was powered to detect HbA1c change, not myocardial infarction. No single trial was big enough to detect a rare CV harm signal.

Steven Nissen pooled them all (NEJM 2007). 15,560 patients, 42 trials, MI as the endpoint.
- Pooled OR 1.43 (95% CI 1.03, 1.98). 43 percent more heart attacks.
- Pooled OR for CV death 1.64, just shy of significance.

The FDA imposed a black-box warning in 2007 and severely restricted use in 2010. Sales collapsed.

Meta-analysis lesson: TRIALS ARE POWERED FOR EFFICACY, NOT RARE HARMS. To detect a rare adverse event, you need:
- Many trials pooled (large total n)
- OR genuine post-marketing surveillance
- OR a dedicated CV outcomes trial

The Rosiglitazone case directly led to the FDA 2008 requirement that all new diabetes drugs run pre-approval CV outcome trials (CVOTs). Every modern SGLT2 inhibitor and GLP-1 agonist has CV-safety MA data because of this case.

Other echoes:
- Vioxx (Topol/Curfman pooled MAs detected the signal)
- COX-2 class broadly
- Antipsychotics in elderly with dementia

Sources:
- Nissen SE, Wolski K. NEJM 2007;356:2457-71
- Singh S et al. JAMA 2007;298:1189-95 (independent replication MA)
- Home PD et al. Lancet 2009;373:2125-35 (RECORD trial)
- FDA briefing document, July 2010

Methodological note: individual trial point estimates illustrative; Nissen 2007 pooled OR is exact published value.

title: They gave diabetics a pill. It lowered blood sugar AND doubled their fat cells. Wait, what...
description:
They gave diabetics a pill. It lowered blood sugar AND doubled their fat cells. Wait, what?

A 2011 Cell Metabolism study out of UT Southwestern just cracked open something most doctors never discuss with their patients.

Researchers tracked fat tissue in real time using a cutting-edge cell-marking system. They gave mice a TZD diabetes drug called rosiglitazone — one of the most widely prescribed insulin sensitizers ever made.

Here's what they found:

• TZDs roughly DOUBLED the creation of brand new fat cells from stem cells

• Fat stem cells were pushed to divide AND mature into full adipocytes at an accelerated rate

• BrdU labeling confirmed new fat cells were being born from a proliferating source

• After chronic use, fat stem cells became EXHAUSTED — losing their ability to self-renew

• The stem cell pool shrank and lost key markers of healthy fat tissue function

• Genes linked to fat formation were dysregulated in ways that could worsen metabolic health long-term

So yes — the drug lowering your blood sugar may simultaneously be reengineering your fat tissue architecture. Like a contractor fixing your plumbing but quietly knocking down load-bearing walls.

The weight gain side effect of TZDs isn't just "eating more." It's your body literally building new fat real estate at the cellular level.

What does this mean for the millions still on these medications? And why does your doctor's prescription pad rarely come with this conversation attached?

What's one question you wish your doctor had answered before putting you on a long-term medication?

シックデイでは、食べていなくても血糖が上がることがあります。一方で、食事量が少ないのに薬をいつも通り使うと、低血糖を起こすこともあります。

この動画では、糖尿病治療中の方に向けて、シックデイの基本対応、水分・食事のとり方、血糖測定の目安、休薬が必要な薬、自己判断で中止してはいけない薬、すぐに受診すべき危険サインについてわかりやすく解説します。

特に、メトホルミン、SGLT2阻害薬、マンジャロ・オゼンピックなどのGLP-1関連薬、インスリンを使用中の方は注意が必要です。

体調不良の時に慌てないために、元気な時から自分専用の「シックデイルール」を主治医と確認しておきましょう。

In this video, I explained how HbA1c helps determine whether your diabetes treatment is working properly or not. HbA1c reflects your average blood sugar level over the last 3 months and is one of the most important tests for diabetic patients.

For example, if your HbA1c was 7.5 before starting treatment, then after 3 months it should ideally reduce by around 0.5 or more. If the value becomes 7 or lower, it usually indicates that your medicines, diet, and lifestyle changes are working effectively.

I also explained why patients should continue monitoring:
• Fasting blood sugar  
• Post meal (after food) sugar  
• Regular HbA1c testing  

Along with medicines, proper diet control, exercise, weight management, and healthy lifestyle habits are extremely important for long-term diabetes control.

• Type 2 diabetes patients

title: Sulphonylureas — Mechanism and Why Hypoglycemia is the Main Concern
description:
Sulphonylureas are oral diabetes drugs
that directly stimulate insulin secretion.

How they work:
- Block ATP-sensitive K+ channels
- Cell membrane depolarises
- Calcium enters beta cell
- Insulin secreted
- Blood glucose improves

Examples:
Gliclazide | Glipizide
Glibenclamide | Glimepiride

Key concern:
Hypoglycemia — stimulates insulin
regardless of glucose level

Caution in:
Renal impairment & elderly
Drug accumulates
→ prolonged hypoglycemia risk

Also watch for:
Weight gain

title: “It Didn’t Work on Me” #why
description:
Source- https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-026-01630-0 

A recent study published in Genome Medicine reveals that genetic variants in the PAM gene, present in roughly ten percent of the population, can significantly reduce a person's response to GLP-1 medications. The PAM gene produces an enzyme responsible for activating metabolic hormones. Researchers discovered that individuals with these specific variations actually have higher circulating levels of the hormone but exhibit a strong biological resistance to it. As a result, the hormone and medications designed to mimic it become far less effective at slowing digestion and regulating blood sugar. When evaluating clinical trial data, the researchers found that patients carrying these PAM variants experienced up to a 44 percent reduction in the therapeutic benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists compared to those without the variant. This unexpected resistance explains why a significant portion of individuals with type 2 diabetes do not see the anticipated improvements from these widely prescribed treatments.

New weight loss drugs may soon go beyond Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound.
Some pipeline obesity medications are reporting weight loss numbers that could change the future of obesity care.

Current medications like semaglutide, Wegovy, tirzepatide, Mounjaro, and Zepbound have already changed how doctors think about obesity treatment. But the next generation may be even more powerful, more personalized, and in some cases faster acting.

title: Medications like Ozempic, Wegovy, and Mounjaro are often misunderstood.They are not shortcuts.
description:
Medications like Ozempic, Wegovy, and Mounjaro are often misunderstood.
They are not shortcuts.
They are disease-modifying therapies grounded in decades of metabolic research.
These medications mimic natural gut hormones that:
• Regulate appetite
• Improve insulin secretion
• Reduce glucagon production
• Improve metabolic health
Clinical trials show:
• Semaglutide averages ~15% body weight reduction
• Tirzepatide averages ~15–21% weight loss
Even more importantly, research shows they can:
• Reduce cardiovascular events
• Improve blood pressure
• Improve triglycerides
• Support kidney protection
However, these medications treat chronic metabolic disease, which means long-term treatment may be necessary.
Lifestyle still matters.
Adequate protein intake and resistance training are essential to preserve muscle mass.
When used thoughtfully with physician guidance, these medications can be powerful tools for improving cardiometabolic health.

description:
🔥 Abnehmspritzen 2026: Was kommt nach Ozempic, Wegovy & Mounjaro?
💉 Tabletten statt Spritzen? Noch stärkere Wirkstoffe? Und was passiert wirklich nach dem Absetzen?
⚠️ Dieses Update solltest du kennen, bevor du über #Abnehmspritzen, #GLP1, #Wegovy, #Ozempic oder #Mounjaro urteilst.
Viele Menschen scheitern beim Abnehmen nicht an fehlender Disziplin – sondern an ihrer Biologie. Genau deshalb verändern #Abnehmspritzen gerade die Medizin: nicht als „Wundermittel“, sondern als ernstzunehmendes Werkzeug in der Behandlung von #Adipositas, #Übergewicht und Stoffwechselproblemen. 🧠🔥
In diesem Video „Abnehmspritzen – Update 2026“ schauen wir medizinisch seriös, verständlich und ohne Hype auf die wichtigsten Entwicklungen rund um #GLP1, #Ozempic, #Wegovy, #Mounjaro, #Semaglutid, #Tirzepatid, #Retatrutid, #CagriSema und neue Tabletten wie #Orforglipron oder #Amycretin. 💊💉
Denn die große Frage lautet nicht nur:
👉 „Wie viel kann man mit #Abnehmspritzen abnehmen?“
Sondern auch:
👉 „Wie gesund ist dieser Gewichtsverlust wirklich?“
👉 „Was passiert mit Muskeln, Hunger, Sättigung und Stoffwechsel?“
👉 „Was passiert nach dem Absetzen?“
👉 „Und für wen sind #Abnehmspritzen wirklich sinnvoll?“ ⚖️
Wir sprechen darüber, warum #GLP1-Medikamente Hunger leiser machen, Sättigung verstärken und Essensgedanken bei vielen Betroffenen deutlich reduzieren können. Für viele Menschen mit #Adipositas ist genau das der eigentliche Durchbruch: Zum ersten Mal kreist nicht mehr der ganze Tag ums Essen. 🧠🍽️
Aber dieses #Update2026 zeigt auch die andere Seite: Je stärker Medikamente wie #Wegovy, #Ozempic, #Mounjaro oder zukünftige Wirkstoffe wie #Retatrutid und #CagriSema werden, desto wichtiger werden ärztliche Begleitung, Eiweiß, Krafttraining, Bewegung, Laborwerte und ein realistischer Langzeitplan. 💪🩺
Denn #Abnehmspritzen können helfen – aber sie ersetzen keine medizinisch begleitete Strategie. Wer Gewicht verliert, verliert nicht automatisch nur Fett. Auch Muskelmasse kann betroffen sein. Deshalb geht es bei seriöser #Abnehmmedizin nicht um „schnell dünn“, sondern um langfristig gesünder, stärker und stabiler. 🌱
Auch Nebenwirkungen gehören ehrlich auf den Tisch: Übelkeit, Erbrechen, Verstopfung oder Durchfall können auftreten. Seltene, aber ernste Risiken wie Gallensteine oder Bauchspeicheldrüsenentzündungen müssen ärztlich eingeordnet werden. Illegale Online-Angebote sind gefährlich – #Abnehmspritzen sind kein harmloser Trend, sondern ein medizinischer Eingriff in den Stoffwechsel. ⚠️🩺
Besonders wichtig: Was passiert nach dem Absetzen von #GLP1, #Wegovy, #Ozempic oder #Mounjaro? Viele nehmen wieder zu – nicht, weil sie „versagt“ haben, sondern weil Hunger, Sättigung und Stoffwechselregulation wieder stärker werden können. Genau deshalb wird #Adipositas heute zunehmend als chronische Erkrankung verstanden. 🧬
Dieses Video ist für dich, wenn du selbst betroffen bist, jemanden kennst oder einfach verstehen willst, wohin sich die Behandlung von #Übergewicht, #Adipositas und #Abnehmen ab dem Jahr 2026 entwickelt. 💙

description:
Un paciente entra en una farmacia de Miami el 5 de mayo de 2026 y recibe la misma respuesta de siempre: no hay stock. Detrás de ese estante vacío se libra la guerra comercial más lucrativa de la historia moderna.
Novo Nordisk contra Eli Lilly. No es solo medicina, es la fiebre del oro del siglo veintiuno. Los daneses de Novo Nordisk golpearon primero con Wegovy, creando un fenómeno cultural global. Pero Eli Lilly no se quedó mirando. El 2 de mayo de 2026, la firma estadounidense reportó ingresos récord impulsados por Zepbound, un competidor que devora la cuota de mercado a una velocidad aterradora. 💉
La comparativa es fascinante. Novo Nordisk posee la ventaja del pionero. Sin embargo, Eli Lilly juega al estilo de las grandes tecnológicas. Mientras los daneses sufren cuellos de botella en sus plantas de Dinamarca, Lilly ha invertido 18 mil millones de dólares en complejos industriales masivos que operan a plena capacidad este trimestre. Es escala contra tradición. Uno inventó el mercado, el otro construye la maquinaria pesada para dominarlo por completo. 📈
La lección de MBA aquí es brutal: el producto no es el rey; la logística lo es. Novo Nordisk descubrió que la patente más deseada del mundo no sirve si tus fábricas no dan abasto. Eli Lilly ha demostrado que la agresividad financiera en infraestructura es el mejor ataque. El lanzamiento de su pastilla Foundayo el 1 de abril de 2026 ha terminado por inclinar la balanza. 🌎
Hoy, Eli Lilly se consolida como la primera farmacéutica de un billón de dólares. La victoria no será para quien tenga la mejor molécula, sino para quien logre llenar cada estante del planeta primero. 💊

title: 노보 노디스크 경구 인슐린 실패에서 본삼천당제약의 경구 인슐린 성공의 힌트
description:
[영상 개요] 왜 세계 1위 노보 노디스크는 포기하고, 삼천당제약은 도전하는가?
전 세계 당뇨 치료제 시장의 절대 강자, 노보 노디스크가 수조 원을 쏟아붓고도 2019년 결국 폐기한 프로젝트가 있습니다. 바로 '먹는 인슐린(Oral Insulin)'입니다.

약효가 없어서였을까요? 아닙니다. 임상 2상에서 주사제와 동등한 효과를 증명하고도 그들이 멈출 수밖에 없었던 이유는 바로 '상업적 원가 구조' 때문이었습니다.

오늘 이콘인사이트에서는 삼천당제약의 S-PASS 기술이 어떻게 노보 노디스크가 넘지 못한 '58배의 원재료 장벽'을 허물려 하는지, 그리고 최근 성공한 세마글루타이드 BE 스터디가 경구 인슐린 임상(SCD0503)에 어떤 과학적 확신을 주는지 그 구조를 정밀 분석합니다.

[상세 분석 내용]
노보 노디스크의 뼈아픈 교훈: 주사제 대비 58배의 원료를 투입해야 했던 SNAC 기술의 한계와 가격 통제 정책이 맞물린 상업적 실패를 분석합니다.

S-PASS의 차별성: 세포 사이와 세포 통과라는 두 가지 경로를 동시에 활용하여 '음식물 간섭'을 정면 돌파하는 메커니즘을 설명합니다.

임상 SCD0503의 정밀함: 1형 당뇨 환자 대상, 정상혈당 클램프 기법, 6기간 교차 설계 등 데이터 오차를 극단적으로 줄인 삼천당제약의 전략을 짚어봅니다.

성공의 열쇠: 결국 '흡수율'이 원가를 얼마나 낮출 수 있느냐가 글로벌 빅파마와의 파트너십을 결정짓는 핵심 변수가 될 것입니다.

title: 1.000€-Aus & Rheinmetall-Absturz: Commerzbank, Novo Nordisk, Realty, Zoetis, TransMedics | #16
description:
In Folge 16 von https://wonderl.ink/@economyfirstsprechen wir über eine volle Earnings-Folge mit spannenden Aktien, starken Rücksetzern und einigen überraschenden Wendungen.



Zum Start geht es um die geplatzte steuerfreie *1.000-Euro-Prämie* und warum die Bundesländer im Bundesrat nicht mitgezogen haben. Danach schauen wir auf die *Commerzbank*, den Übernahmekampf mit *UniCredit*, starke Zahlen, Dividende, Stellenabbau und die Frage, warum die Bank eigenständig bleiben will.



Anschließend sprechen wir über *Realty Income*, Umsatzwachstum, AFFO, Dividendenqualität, Portfolioauslastung und das neue Joint Venture mit *Apollo*.

Danach wird es spannend bei *Zoetis*: Der Tierpharma-Weltmarktführer ist nach schwächeren Zahlen deutlich gefallen. Wir diskutieren, ob nur ein Quartal enttäuscht hat oder ob das starke Narrativ rund um Preissetzungsmacht beschädigt ist.



Ein großes Thema ist außerdem *Rheinmetall*. Trotz hoher Auftragsbestände kam die Aktie nach den Zahlen unter Druck. Wir sprechen über Umsatz, Marge, NATO-Aufrüstung, Bewertung, Analystenabstufung und die Frage, ob nach der Rallye noch Luft nach oben bleibt.



Mit *TransMedics* bringt Marin einen spannenden Wachstumswert aus Organtransplantation und medizinischer Logistik mit. Es geht um warme Organperfusion, eigene Flugzeugflotte, hohe Investitionen, Insideraktivitäten und langfristige Chancen.



Zum Schluss schauen wir auf *Novo Nordisk*. Nach langer Schwäche zeigen die Zahlen erste positive Signale. Thema sind Abnehmspritzen, GLP-1-Pille, Konkurrenz durch Eli Lilly, Preisdruck, Dividende und die Frage, ob Novo langsam den Boden gefunden hat.

title: How we respond in the big moments, is everything.
description:
In this clip, keynote speaker Chris Dyer tells the story of Johnson & Johnson CEO James Burke and the 1982 Tylenol crisis, one of the most studied decision moments in business history. Seven people in Chicago died after taking cyanide-laced capsules. The FBI said it was localized. The lawyers said J&J had no liability. Burke recalled 31 million bottles anyway, a $100 million bet (over $300 million in today’s dollars) on a one-page company credo that said customers come first.
Tylenol was 17% of Johnson & Johnson’s income. Wall Street declared the brand dead. Within a year, it had recovered 92% of its market share. The Harvard Business Review called it the greatest comeback in business history.
Chris Dyer, named the #1 Leadership Speaker to Follow in 2026 by MSN.com, unpacks what Burke’s decision teaches leaders about crisis response, values alignment, and why the moments that test your stated principles are the ones that define your culture. This story comes from Chris Dyer’s bestselling book Moments That Matter: See, Shape, and Scale What Counts (March 2026), which identifies seven types of moments that shape careers, teams, and organizations.
Chris Dyer is also ranked #1 Leadership Speaker on Culture by Inc. Magazine and #15 on the Global Gurus Top 30 for Organizational Culture. Neste episódio do Revelando o Capital, Revel mostra como uma pequena farmácia do século XIX se transformou em um império global da indústria farmacêutica, com bilhões de dólares em receita, presença internacional e uma trajetória marcada por inovação, aquisições e grandes controvérsias.

A origem da Johnson & Johnson começa em 1873, quando Robert Wood Johnson e George Seabury criaram uma farmácia voltada para produtos médicos em Nova York. A partir do contato com as ideias de Joseph Lister sobre cirurgias antissépticas, nasceu a visão que levaria a empresa a revolucionar o mercado de materiais cirúrgicos estéreis e primeiros socorros.

Johnson & Johnson: da inovação médica ao IPO
Com o crescimento da companhia, a Johnson & Johnson passou a criar produtos que se tornaram parte da vida cotidiana, como Band-Aid, fio dental, cotonetes, talco infantil e kits médicos. O episódio também mostra como a empresa atravessou guerras, pandemias, a Grande Depressão e abriu capital na Bolsa de Nova York sob o ticker JNJ, consolidando-se como uma das gigantes globais da saúde.

Mas por trás da força da marca, a história da Johnson & Johnson também inclui crises profundas. O vídeo revisita o caso Tylenol de 1982, uma das maiores crises corporativas da indústria farmacêutica, além das polêmicas envolvendo talco, opioides, próteses, telas cirúrgicas e processos judiciais que desafiaram a reputação da companhia.

Kenvue, Tylenol e o futuro da Johnson & Johnson
Nos últimos anos, a separação da divisão de consumo e a criação da Kenvue mudaram completamente o rumo da empresa. Marcas populares como Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine e Band-Aid deixaram de fazer parte diretamente da Johnson & Johnson, enquanto a companhia passou a concentrar sua estratégia em medicamentos de alta complexidade, tecnologia médica, oncologia, neurologia e soluções cardiovasculares.

title: How Johnson & Johnson Knew Their Baby Powder Contained Asbestos — For Decades 👶☠️
description:
Johnson & Johnson's baby powder — one of the most recognized consumer products in the world — has been the subject of tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging that the talc-based product contained asbestos and contributed to cancer. Internal company documents dating to at least 1971, revealed through litigation discovery, showed that J&J's own testing had detected asbestos fibers in its talc supply.

Despite this knowledge, the company continued marketing baby powder for decades without disclosing the contamination risk to consumers. Multiple studies have linked talc exposure to ovarian cancer when the product is used for feminine hygiene — one of its most heavily marketed applications. Thousands of women have filed lawsuits alleging that years of baby powder use contributed to their cancer diagnoses.

In an attempt to manage its legal liability, J&J employed a strategy known as the "Texas Two-Step." In 2021, the company created a subsidiary called LTL Management, transferred all talc-related legal liabilities to it, and then placed that subsidiary into bankruptcy — effectively shielding J&J's $400 billion parent company from paying full damages. The strategy was challenged in court, with critics calling it an abuse of the bankruptcy system.

J&J discontinued its talc-based baby powder globally in 2023, switching to a cornstarch formula. The company has proposed a $8.9 billion settlement fund for talc claimants, which remains under litigation.

title: Jack Johnson, Hermanos Gutiérrez - Drink The Water (from the SURFILMUSIC Soundtrack)
description:
Jack Johnson announces SURFILMUSIC, a new documentary chronicling his evolution from surfer to filmmaker to world-renowned musician. The film makes its World Premiere today at SXSW ahead of a special concert tonight at Stubb’s in Austin, Texas, where Johnson and his band will perform with Hermanos Gutiérrez.

SURFILMUSIC traces how Johnson’s early years making surf films with close friends became a foundation for a much broader creative life, capturing moments in and out of the water that later surfaced in his songwriting. Blending rare footage from those formative surf films and Johnson's personal and family archives with present-day reflections, the film weaves together how lived experience, friendship, and exploration shaped the sound and stories behind the music. Directed by Emmett Malloy, featuring Jack Johnson, Kelly Slater, Rob Machado, Gerry Lopez, Chris Malloy, G Love, Ben Harper, John Florence, Tamayo Perry, Emmett Malloy, Kim Johnson, and more, with a beautiful score by Jack Johnson and Hermanos Gutiérrez.

In addition to the new film, Johnson has announced a companion double album, SURFILMUSIC Soundtrack and 4-Tracks, arriving May 15 via Brushfire Records. The soundtrack features the film’s original score by Jack Johnson and Hermanos Gutiérrez alongside remastered selections from Johnson’s early four-track recordings. 4-Tracks presents a deeper dive into the archival music from Johnson’s personal tapes, including raw recordings and previously unreleased gems from his earliest days making music.

The first track from the soundtrack is a new rendition of “Drink the Water w/ Hermanos Gutiērrez,” and is available now on all digital streaming platforms.

Esperou. Em 1886, assim que pôde, fundou a Johnson & Johnson com os irmãos, em um prédio simples, com 14 funcionários.

Criou os primeiros curativos cirúrgicos estéreis da história.

Faleceu em 1910 com mais de 1.200 funcionários e um legado que salvou milhões de vidas.

O menino invisível virou o homem que mudou a medicina para sempre.

description:
The Johnson & Johnson family built a three hundred eighty-four billion dollar healthcare empire, then deliberately gave away control through charitable trusts, fired the founder's grandson from leadership, and ensured descendants would never manage the pharmaceutical company bearing their name.

-------------------

-------------------

Johnson & Johnson commands a three hundred eighty-four billion dollar market capitalization as one of America's most valuable healthcare companies, yet the founding family's collective ownership barely registers at 0.19 percent while institutional investors control seventy-four percent of all outstanding shares.

The company reported 94.2 billion dollars in revenue for twenty twenty-five, but the Johnson family no longer controls the enterprise founded in eighteen eighty-six by three brothers in a New Brunswick, New Jersey factory with just fourteen employees making sterile surgical dressings.

The Vanguard Group holds between 9.5 and 9.8 percent worth up to two hundred thirty-seven billion dollars, BlackRock controls 8.3 to 8.6 percent representing two hundred eight billion dollars, and State Street owns 5.5 percent worth approximately one hundred thirty-three billion dollars.

Together these three asset management giants control roughly twenty-four percent of Johnson & Johnson—nearly five hundred seventy billion dollars voted by professional fund managers who have never heard of Robert Wood Johnson I and have no emotional attachment to founding family legacy.

The twelve-member board of directors includes executives from Lockheed Martin, Best Buy, and J.P. Morgan, but no Johnsons sit among them, with current CEO Joaquin Duato earning his position through thirty years of pharmaceutical division competence rather than birth into the founding family.

Robert Wood Johnson II, known as "The General," took Johnson & Johnson public in nineteen forty-four at 37.50 dollars per share when annual sales totaled approximately ninety-five million dollars, then established trusts fragmenting collective ownership so thoroughly that no single branch could ever again control the company.

The most consequential moment occurred in nineteen sixty-three when Philip B. Hofmann became chairman and CEO—the first non-family member to lead the company since its eighteen eighty-seven incorporation, marking the end of seventy-six years of dynastic control.

Hofmann's ascension followed The General firing his own son Robert Wood Johnson III in nineteen sixty-five, signaling that professional managers who earned positions through merit would replace heirs who happened to share the founder's blood.

When Robert Wood Johnson II died January thirtieth, nineteen sixty-eight, his will bequeathed 10,204,377 shares worth over 1.2 billion dollars to the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation rather than to his children, creating what became the nation's largest philanthropy devoted exclusively to improving American health with assets now exceeding 13.6 billion dollars.

J. Seward Johnson I married Barbara Piasecka, his former chambermaid, in nineteen seventy-one, then left his entire four hundred to five hundred million dollar estate to her upon his death in nineteen eighty-three, completely disinheriting five of his six children and triggering an ugly legal battle that settled for approximately three hundred million to Barbara.

Robert Wood Johnson IV "Woody" inherited 3.4 billion dollars in Johnson & Johnson stock despite working at the company for only one summer, purchasing the New York Jets in two thousand for six hundred thirty-five million dollars alongside brother Christopher.

On May fourth, twenty twenty-three, Johnson & Johnson spun off Kenvue containing Band-Aid, Tylenol, and Johnson's Baby Powder, with Kimberly-Clark acquiring the consumer division for 48.7 billion dollars within 2.5 years—ending one hundred thirty-five years of the founding family's connection to the products that made their name famous.

title: MERCK詐騙警示：勿信高回報穩賺不賠陷阱
description:
#MERCK詐騙 #MERCK 被詐騙之後不要慌，要先冷靜的去保存跟詐騙集團的聊天記錄還有銀行的轉帳記錄，我之前也是被這樣的手法騙了，後來找到恩人然後經過他的 幫助現在已經把被騙的錢追回來，如果你也被騙了可以聯絡我LINE：W03816，告訴你怎麼拿回來，在這裡勸大家不懂投資的不要去亂投資。


要注意網路上看到的投資廣告或網友傳來的投資訊息，標榜「#保證獲利」、「#沒有風險」、「#穩賺不賠」訊息，這些都是詐騙集團常用的#釣魚手法，目的就是要誇大吸引被害人，以便進一步用於金融詐騙。務必提高警覺，勿輕易受騙，勿點可疑連結！
1.歹徒會利用FB、IG、YT、Google及簡訊等管道以股市名人、財經專家等人名義投放假投資廣告，或在交友軟體App假交友，宣稱保證獲利、穩賺不賠且利潤豐厚來吸引被害人。
2.當被害者上鉤後，歹徒會介紹其他「客服、老師、助理」同夥加 LINE 聯繫或加入LINE投資群組，並提供假投資網站或App給被害人註冊、下載安裝及操作，此時LINE群組內不斷有其他假學員獲利貼文。
3.自稱「客服、老師、助理」的歹徒會提供 銀行帳號 給被害人入金投資，或以「參與抽股」、「系統中籤」等各種理由要求被害人補足入金。
4.初期帳面顯示獲利（實際是歹徒於後臺控制），引誘您加碼投入大筆資金，有時可出金微薄獲利，但出金款項其實是其他被害人匯款的，可能會導致您銀行帳戶被警示。
5.當被害人要提領獲利時，以各種理由拖延（需繳保證金、IP異常、洗碼量不足等）或是直接凍結帳號、失去聯繫，就是「不出金」。

title: Dr  Rasha Kelej visit to H E  Madam ZITA OLIGUI NGUEMA, the First Lady of Gabon 2026!
description:
Senator Dr. Rasha Kelej, B.Sc Pharma, MBA, Chief Executive Officer, Merck Foundation. My views are personal.

“It was a great honor to visit my dear sister, H.E. Madam ZITA OLIGUI NGUEMA, the First Lady of Gabon and Ambassador of the ‘Merck Foundation More Than a Mother’ to officially launch our long-term partnership to build healthcare capacity, support girls’ education and break the infertility stigma in Gabon.

We also visited the Ma Bannière Foundation to witness the wonderful work that the First Lady of Gabon is doing. I am very proud to share that through our partnership, we have provided 16 scholarships for our local healthcare providers who will be the future healthcare experts of Gabon, who have either graduated, undergoing or will be starting soon the Merck Foundation scholarships of training in critical and underserved specialties such as Fertility, Embryology, Oncology, Diabetes and Hypertension.

I am also very happy to share that together with The First Lady of Gabon, we are also supporting girl education by providing annual scholarships to support the education of 40 high-performing yet underprivileged schoolgirls, till they graduate, so that they can reach their potentials and achieve their dreams”

Dr. Rasha Kelej
CEO of Merck Foundation
President of “More Than a Mother”

title: I’m happy to share the photos from my visit to Kenya Merck Foundation Educating Linda Program 2026
description:
Senator Dr. Rasha Kelej, B.Sc Pharma, MBA, Chief Executive Officer, Merck Foundation. My views are personal.

"At the Kenya state house, It was a great honor to visit my dear sister, H.E. Mrs. RACHEL RUTO, the First Lady of Kenya and recognize her for her great efforts as the Ambassador of the 'Merck Foundation More Than a Mother' and to officially launch our long-term partnership to build healthcare capacity, support girls' education and break the infertility stigma in Kenya.

Though our long term partnership, we have provided more than 328 scholarships to local Kenyan healthcare providers in 44 critical and underserved medical specialties. These doctors, who are Merck Foundation Alumni are transforming the patient care landscape and building the healthcare capacity of Kenya. 

I am also proud that, as part of the Educating Linda program, in partnership with Voice of Children Foundation of Kenya First Lady, we have provided 47 Annual Scholarships and Grants to young girls from Kenya.”

Dr. Rasha Kelej 
CEO of Merck Foundation 
President of “More Than a Mother”

"MERCK FOUNDATION PRESENTS OUR AFRICA TV Program by Merck Foundation Ep.5- Breaking Infertility Stigma

Concept, Director & Executive Producer:                                           
Senator, Dr. Rasha Kelej                                                                           
CEO of Merck Foundation

Host
SENATOR, DR. RASHA KELEJ

CO-HOST
BRIAN MULONDO

“I’m very excited to share with you all the 5th episode for ""Our Africa by Merck Foundation", a TV Program which I have conceptualized, directed and produced. I strongly believe that media, fashion and art should have a purpose beyond entertainment and looking good and can raise awareness about issues such as Diabetes Awareness, Breaking Infertility Stigma, Ending Child Marriage, stopping FGM, stopping GBV, Supporting Girl Education and women empowerment, among other social and health issues affecting the continent. Together we can create a culture shift. Stay tuned to watch “OUR AFRICA by Merck Foundation” TV program.

‘Our Africa TV program’ which is hosted by myself and co-hosted Brian Mulondo, is our your TV channels in Ghana, Kenya & Uganda.
-Every Saturday @ 5:30 pm (EAT) on KTN, Kenya
-Every Sunday @ 6:30 pm (EAT) on NTV Uganda
-Every Sunday @ 2 pm (GMT) on GHOne TV, Ghana

Stay tuned for more information!

Concept, Director & Executive Producer,
Senator, Dr. Rasha Kelej
CEO of Merck Foundation"

title: Open Mic: Next in Health series - Agentic AI
description:
Many thanks to everyone who joined us for our latest Open Mic session – a timely discussion on how agentic AI could help reduce complexity across the clinical trial lifecycle and support a more efficient future for drug development.

The event opened with a plenary presentation by Dr. Petra Jantzer, Managing Director, Global Client Account Partner, Accenture.

Here are some of the key takeaways from the conversation on turning AI potential into practical impact in clinical trials:

✔️ From experimentation to implementation: Agentic AI offers promising opportunities to automate and coordinate complex workflows, but real-world value depends on clear use cases, strong validation and deployment models that work in regulated environments.

✔️ Automation-ready vs. human-critical: From protocol design and site activation to patient recruitment and study management, the discussion explored where AI agents can meaningfully reduce manual burden – and where expert human oversight remains essential.

✔️ Trust, governance and data quality: For agentic AI to move beyond pilots, pharma teams and technology partners need to address key challenges around data readiness, transparency, compliance, accountability and integration into existing clinical operations.

The discussion offered a practical look at where agentic AI can support clinical trials today, where expectations need to be tested carefully and what it will take to move from promising technology to trusted implementation.

🙏 A huge thank you to Accenture for sponsoring this edition of Open Mic, and to our expert panel for sharing their perspectives and experiences:

title: India Remains A Strategic Market, Says Novartis India Chief
description:
In his first and exclusive interview after Novartis AG’s decision to sell its stake in Novartis India Limited, Novartis India Country President and Managing Director Amitabh Dube tells Business Today that the transaction represents a structural shift in the company’s global strategy rather than an exit from the country. He says India remains a strategic market for the Swiss drugmaker, with innovation, research and development operations continuing to expand even as the listed entity changes ownership. Novartis AG will continue its operations in India through its fully owned subsidiary, Novartis Healthcare Private Limited. Dube adds that scientists in India contribute to nearly every molecule commercialised globally by Novartis. The company is also preparing to launch highly targeted radioligand therapy for prostate cancer treatment in India while continuing to work with stakeholders to improve patient access to innovative medicines. The company’s priorities going forward include oncology, cardio-renal-metabolic diseases, immunology and neuroscience, he said.

title: Novartis  India Reshuffle
description:
🚨 **Big Pharma Exit. Big PE Entry. A Defining Moment for Indian Pharma.**

The Swiss giant **Novartis AG** has signed a pact to sell its **70.68% majority stake** in **Novartis India Limited** to a consortium led by **ChrysCapital**.

💰 **Deal Size:** ~₹1,446 crore
📌 **Open Offer Price:** ₹860.64 per share
📈 **Market Reaction:** ~20% stock surge post announcement

Here’s why this matters 👇

---

### 🔎 What’s Happening?

▪️ Novartis AG exits its listed India commercial arm
▪️ ChrysCapital-led consortium acquires controlling stake
▪️ Mandatory open offer to public shareholders under SEBI norms
▪️ Potential board reshuffle & possible rebranding ahead

---

### 🎯 Why Is Novartis Exiting?

▪️ Global strategic pivot toward **innovative, patented medicines**
▪️ Portfolio simplification and capital reallocation
▪️ Focus on high-growth R&D-driven markets

This is consistent with Big Pharma’s global shift from legacy commercial businesses to high-margin specialty innovation.

---

### 💼 Why This Is a Big Bet for PE

▪️ ChrysCapital’s **first majority control deal in Indian pharma**
▪️ Opportunity for operational turnaround + brand revitalization
▪️ Scope for margin expansion & sharper go-to-market strategy
▪️ Potential multi-year value creation story

Private equity confidence in Indian healthcare remains strong.

---

### 📊 What It Signals for the Industry

✔️ MNCs reassessing commercial models in emerging markets
✔️ Indian pharma assets remain attractive for financial sponsors
✔️ Domestic consumption & specialty growth story intact
✔️ Potential for more carve-outs & strategic exits ahead

---

🔥 **Bottom Line:**
This isn’t just a stake sale. It’s a strategic realignment.
Global Pharma consolidates. Indian PE scales.

The next 3–5 years will determine whether this becomes a case study in pharma value creation.

What’s your take — strategic brilliance or timing play? 👇

title: How Novartis Used the Super Bowl for Health Behavior Change
description:
Super Bowl marketing strategy just got a masterclass — five CMOs who advertised in Super Bowl 2026 reveal exactly what worked, what didn't, and what's next. Subscribe for weekly marketing and brand strategy insights.
Whether you're planning a big-game campaign or trying to get more ROI from experiential marketing, this episode breaks down the real playbook behind brands like Ritz, EOS, Novartis, Cadillac F1, and Tree Hut.

✅ How top brands turned Super Bowl weekend into content production days
✅ Why surround sound strategy matters more than the 30-second spot itself
✅ The shift from social graph to interest graph — and what it means for brand relevance
✅ Real ROI data: in-store sales lift, behavior change, and brand recall metrics
✅ Advice for first-time Super Bowl advertisers from veterans and rookies alike

Jim Stengel and Gary Vaynerchuk sit down with five CMOs and marketing leaders — Stephen Saenen (Ritz/Mondelez), Soyoung Kang (EOS), Gail Horwood (Novartis), Ahmed "Meddy" Iqbal (Cadillac F1), and Luis Garcia (Tree Hut) — for their eighth annual Super Bowl debrief. This isn't a generic ad review. It's an operator-level breakdown of how each brand approached strategy, creative development, celebrity usage, retail activation, and experiential marketing around the biggest advertising moment of the year.

Stephen Saenen shares how Ritz doubled down on its "Salty Club" platform in year two, using multiple celebrities while keeping brand recall front and center. Soyoung Kang explains how EOS leveraged a fan-driven insight — that their products smell like cupcakes — into a partnership with the "Is It Cake?" franchise, driving massive social engagement before the spot even aired. Gail Horwood walks through how Novartis built an integrated health behavior change campaign around prostate cancer screening, using authentic NFL storytelling with Gronk and Coach Arians. Ahmed Iqbal reveals how the Cadillac F1 team innovated the traditional livery reveal by pairing their Super Bowl debut with a Times Square activation and a Shot on iPhone campaign in Bahrain — all within 90 days of being hired. And Luis Garcia describes how Tree Hut stayed true to its social-first, creator-driven identity on the biggest stage in advertising.

Gary Vaynerchuk ties it all together with a bold prediction: within five years, a brand's top-performing organic social post will air as a Super Bowl spot — black bars and all. The conversation explores why volume in content creation is not "spray and pray," why trial and sampling are massively underrated by CPG brands, and how the interest-graph algorithm era is finally forcing marketers back to the fundamentals of relevance.

Scroll down to the timestamps to jump straight to each brand's deep dive or Gary's prediction about the future of Super Bowl advertising.

title: PDS Implantation Step-by-Step (Velodrome, Roche), Eye Clinic Sulzbach
description:
This video demonstrates the step-by-step implantation of the Port Delivery System (PDS, Roche)  within the Velodrome study. The PDS is a refillable, transsclerally implanted ocular device that enables continuous intravitreal delivery of ranibizumab, representing a novel treatment approach for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).
The video illustrates the key surgical steps of implantation, including technical nuances, operative details, and practical tips from clinical experience. 
The Velodrome study is a randomized multicenter trial with a follow-up period of 1.5 years, and the Eye Clinic Sulzbach is one of the European study centers. After a single fill, the implant provides sustained drug delivery over several months. Eligible patients include those with a diagnosis of exudative AMD within the past nine months, a demonstrated response to therapy (at least three intravitreal injections within six months), and a visual acuity of at least 34 ETDRS letters (≥ 0.1).
In real-world practice, higher injection frequency correlates with better visual outcomes. The PDS addresses this key limitation by providing continuous drug exposure while reducing treatment burden, potentially representing a significant advancement in long-term AMD management.
🔬 A promising step toward long-acting, patient-friendly therapy in AMD.

In this clip from StarTalk, Neil deGrasse Tyson explains the leading theory of the Moon’s origin — the giant impact with Theia.

According to the discussion, the debris from that collision likely accumulated just outside Earth’s Roche Limit — the boundary where gravity can overcome tidal forces. Inside that limit, material cannot coalesce.

At the time of formation, the Moon would have appeared up to 20 times larger in the sky. Since then, it has been slowly spiraling away from Earth at about 1.5 inches per year.

title: Why is Oxford-AstraZeneca Vaccine Looking Like India’s Best Shot for COVID?
description:
Even as India battles a big spike in COVID cases, forcing some states to reimpose certain restrictions on people's movements, the good news is that vaccine developers are inching towards success in a rapid pace.





Recently, the COVID-19 vaccine being developed by the University of Oxford and Swedish-British pharma AstraZeneca was announced to be 70 percent effective after a large-scale trial. This of course comes on the heels of a string of announcements from other research groups:

     
     
  •  Pfizer's announcement from 9 November, of the interim results of its candidate vaccine proving to be more than 90 percent effective (which they later revised to 95 percent),
     
     
  •  Russia's announcement that came on 11 November, on Sputnik V showing 92 percent efficacy in late-stage trials,
     
     
  •  And Moderna's announcement from 16 November about its candidate's 94.5 percent efficacy.
     
     



And not to mention India's very own candidate — COVAXIN being developed by Bharat Biotech, who on 23 November said that the vaccine is expected to be 60 percent efficacious.

title: Klage gegen Impfstoffhersteller Astra Zeneca: BGH stärkt Auskunftsrechte von Betroffenen | 10.03.26
description:
Vor deutschen Gerichten sind Klagen gegen Impfstoffhersteller bisher oft gescheitert. Nun hat eine Zahnärztin aus Mainz einen Teilerfolg errungen.

„Auf der rechten Seite, da hör ich gar nichts!“ Das berichtet Zahnärztin Pia Aksoy aus Mainz. Sie ist auf dem rechten Ohr taub. „Ich kann zwar meinen Alltag bewältigen, aber es ist eine Einschränkung, die immer da ist und die auch nicht mehr verschwinden wird.“

Ein vollständiger Hörverlust

Pia Aksoy führt den Hörverlust auf eine Corona-Impfung mit dem Impfstoff Vaxzevria von Astra Zeneca zurück. Als die ersten Impfstoffe zum Jahreswechsel 2020/2021 auf den Markt kamen, ließ sich Pia Aksoy schnell impfen, bereits im März 2021 war das.  Sie ist sich sicher, dass die Impfung mit dem Impfstoff Vaxzevria die Ursache hierfür war. Nichts anderes komme in Frage.

Pia Aksoy macht den Impfstoff-Hersteller Astra Zeneca für ihren Hörschaden verantwortlich. Sie hatten deshalb geklagt und will umfassende Auskunft über bekannte Risiken des Corona-Impfstoffs. Außerdem verlangt sie 150.000 Euro Schmerzensgeld und weiteren Schadensersatz.

Keine hohen Hürden für Informationen

Durch die Instanzen klagte sie bis zum Bundesgerichtshof und hat jetzt einen Teilerfolg erzielt. Der BGH sagt: Klägerinnen und Kläger brauchen Informationen von den Pharmafirmen über bekannte Impfstoffrisiken. Sonst hätten mögliche Impfgeschädigte nie eine Chance auf eine erfolgreiche Klage. Die Hürden für einen Informationsanspruch dürften nicht zu hoch sein. Das habe auch der Gesetzgeber so gewollt. Stephan Seiters, Vorsitzender Richter des sechsten Zivilsenats, betonte bei der Urteilsverkündung: Die Geschädigte müsse zwar mehr vortragen als einen bloßen Verdacht, dass der Impfstoff die Ursache für den Gesundheitsschaden sei. Es reiche aber aus, wenn „Anhaltspunkte“ für die Ursächlichkeit vorliegen. Es dürfe da keine zu hohen Anforderungen geben. Sogar wenn mehr dagegenspreche als dafür, dass ein Impfstoff die Ursache für Gesundheitsschäden ist, müsse es Informationen vom Hersteller geben können. Es reiche, dass der Gesundheitsschaden durch das Impfen plausibel ist.

Der BGH hat den Fall nun an die unteren Instanzen zurückverwiesen. Pia Aksoy ist zuversichtlich: „Jetzt sind wir schon so weit gekommen und jetzt gehen wir voller Kraft und voller Zuversicht diesen Weg weiter, damit am Ende die Gerechtigkeit siegt.“

Umfassende Informationen für die Betroffenen

Die heutige Entscheidung bedeutet allerdings nicht, dass Pia Aksoy automatisch gewinnt. Auf jeden Fall hat das BGH-Urteil eine allgemeine Bedeutung dafür, was Impfstoffhersteller an Informationen herausgeben müssen. Der Bundesgerichtshof sagt: Wenn ein Informationsanspruch bestehe, müssen Pharma-Unternehmen auch umfassende Informationen über die Risiken eines Impfstoffs zur Verfügung stellen – und nicht nur Informationen zum einzelnen Krankheitsfall einer Klägerin oder eines Klägers.

Nutzen und Risiken müssen abgewogen werden

Ob Astra Zeneca am Ende Schmerzensgeld und Schadensersatz zahlen muss, würde von einer Abwägung abhängen – zwischen dem Nutzen und dem Risiko einer Astra Zeneca-Impfung während der Corona-Pandemie. Waren die Impfstoffrisiken damals angesichts der Pandemiegefahren hinnehmbar? Durfte die Nutzen-Risiko-Bewertung also zugunsten von Astra Zeneca ausfallen? Das ist die inhaltliche Frage, die ein Gericht im Fall von Pia Aksoy beantworten müsste, damit Geldansprüche möglich sind. Der BGH hat bei der Urteilsverkündung angedeutet, dass die unteren Instanzen auch bei dieser Frage Rechtsfehler gemacht haben. Die Anforderungen daran, was die Klägerin zur Nutzen-Risiko-Bewertung vortragen muss, seien ebenfalls zu streng gewesen. 

Der Anwalt von Astra Zeneca wollte sich nach der Urteilsverkündung in Karlsruhe nicht äußern. Das Unternehmen betonte in einer schriftlichen Stellungnahme, dass die Sicherheit der Patientinnen und Patienten „höchste Priorität“ habe. In der Pandemie hätten Zulassungsbehörden weltweit festgestellt, „dass der Nutzen der Impfung die Risiken äußerst seltener potenzieller Nebenwirkungen überwiegt.“ 

Bisher sind die meisten Klagen wegen Corona-Impfungen vor deutschen Gerichten gescheitert. Die Klage von Pia Aksoy ist die erste gegen einen Impfstoffhersteller, die vor dem obersten deutschen Zivilgericht landete.

title: How AstraZeneca and Decision Lab Built a Strategic Digital Twin for Multi-Region Capacity Planning
description:
Discover how AstraZeneca, in partnership with Decision Lab, transformed its supply chain strategy from reactive, spreadsheet-based forecasting to a proactive, evidence-driven decision-making powerhouse.

Bristol-Myers Squibb Company discovers, develops, licenses, manufactures, markets, distributes, and sells biopharmaceutical products worldwide. The company's products include Opdivo for various anti-cancer indications; Opdivo Qvantig, a subcutaneous PD-1 inhibitor for solid tumorsr; Orencia for active rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis; Yervoy for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma; Reblozyl to treat anemia; Breyanzi for the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma; Opdualag for the treatment of unresectable or metastatic melanoma; and Camzyos to treat symptomatic obstructive HCM to improve functional capacity and symptom. In addition, it offers Eliquis for a reduction in risk of stroke/systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment of DVT/PE; Revlimid, an oral immunomodulatory drug to treat multiple myeloma; Pomalyst/Imnovid for multiple myeloma; Sprycel for Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia; and Abraxane for the treatment of breast cancer. Further, it provides Augtyro for the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC; and NSCLC and pancreatic cancer. It sells products to wholesalers, distributors, specialty pharmacies, and to a lesser extent, retailers, hospitals, clinics, and government agencies. The company was formerly known as Bristol-Myers Company. The company was founded in 1887 and is headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey.

title: Why Psychiatry Is Finally Breaking Free From Dopamine
description:
Psychiatry has long been considered one of the most complex and least understood areas of medicine. While other therapeutic fields have advanced rapidly with clear biomarkers and objective endpoints, mental health has remained rooted in subjective assessments and decades-old treatment approaches.

In this episode, Brandon Li speaks with Ken Kramer, PhD, Vice President and Head of Neuropsychiatry Medical Affairs at Bristol Myers Squibb, about why psychiatry has historically lagged behind and why the field is now entering a new phase of innovation.
Kramer explains how schizophrenia treatment has relied on dopamine receptor-blocking antipsychotics for over 70 years, often forcing patients to trade symptom relief for serious tolerability and safety challenges. He walks through how a new class of treatments, targeting muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, represents a fundamentally different approach, one that may reduce these trade-offs while addressing a broader range of symptoms.
The conversation also explores the structural challenges that have made psychiatric drug development so difficult, from subjective clinical endpoints and high placebo responses to the lack of reliable biomarkers. These barriers pushed many large pharmaceutical companies out of psychiatry for decades.
Now, that trend is reversing. With better scientific understanding, improved trial design, and new mechanisms of action, pharma is re-entering the space with renewed confidence.
Brandon and Ken also discuss the real-world challenges of launching novel treatments, including clinical inertia, physician adoption, and the importance of medical affairs in bridging the gap between approval and actual patient impact.
This episode covers where psychiatry has been, what’s changing, and what it will take to deliver better outcomes for patients living with serious mental illness. 
What You’ll Learn:
Why psychiatry has lagged behind other therapeutic areas in innovation
How dopamine-based antipsychotics shaped schizophrenia treatment for decades
The trade-offs patients face with current standard-of-care therapies
How muscarinic receptor-targeting drugs offer a new approach
Why psychiatric clinical trials are uniquely difficult to design and execute
How subjective endpoints and placebo effects impact drug development
Why pharma companies exited psychiatry and why they’re returning now
The role of medical affairs in driving the adoption of new treatments
How clinical inertia affects real-world patient outcomes
About the Guest:
Ken Kramer has a PhD and Vice President and Head of Neuropsychiatry Medical Affairs at Bristol Myers Squibb. He has spent his entire career focused on psychiatry and neuroscience, with a deep commitment to advancing treatment options for serious mental illness and addressing the stigma associated with these conditions. At BMS, he leads efforts to translate scientific innovation into real-world patient impact across neuropsychiatric disorders.

Bristol-Myers Squibb Company discovers, develops, licenses, manufactures, markets, distributes, and sells biopharmaceutical products worldwide. The company's products include Eliquis for reduction in risk of stroke/systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment of DVT/PE; Opdivo for various anti-cancer indications; Pomalyst/Imnovid for multiple myeloma; Orencia for active rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis; and Sprycel to treat patients with Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia. It also provides Yervoy for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma; Empliciti for the treatment of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; Abecma for the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma; Reblozyl to treat anemia; Opdualag for the treatment of unresectable or metastatic melanoma; and Zeposia to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis. It sells products to wholesalers, distributors, pharmacies, retailers, hospitals, clinics, and government agencies. The company was formerly known as Bristol-Myers Company. Bristol-Myers Squibb Company was founded in 1887 and is headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey.

title: $BMY Bristol Myers Squibb Q3 2025 Earnings Conference Call
description:
10/30/2025 Q&A: 19:23
Bristol-Myers Squibb Company discovers, develops, licenses, manufactures, markets, distributes, and sells biopharmaceutical products worldwide. It offers products for oncology, hematology, immunology, cardiovascular, neuroscience, and other areas. The company's products include Eliquis for reduction in risk of stroke/systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment of DVT/PE; Opdivo for various anti-cancer indications; Pomalyst/Imnovid for multiple myeloma; Orencia for active rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis; and Sprycel to treat patients with Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia.
