title: AbbVie shares early weight loss data for Gubra partnered amylin
description:
00:00:00
In the rapidly evolving field of obesity treatments, AbbVie has stepped into the spotlight with its latest candidate, ABBV-295, also known as GUBamy. This new amylin analogue, developed in partnership with Danish biotech Gubra, is showing early promise in the fight against excess weight. AbbVie acquired the rights to ABBV-295 in 2025, investing $350 million upfront and committing to up to $2.3 billion in milestone payments. What makes ABBV-295 stand out is its potential for less frequent dosing, which could offer a more convenient option for patients. As the fourth major pharmaceutical company in recent months to share results for an amylin analogue, AbbVie’s entry signals growing momentum and competition in this therapeutic area.
00:00:41
Let’s dive into the early clinical data. AbbVie’s Phase I GUC17-01 study tested multiple doses of ABBV-295, ranging from 2 to 14 mg, administered either weekly, every other week, or monthly. The study enrolled 76 adults with a mean BMI under 30, comparing the drug to a placebo. The results are striking: patients receiving weekly injections of ABBV-295 experienced a mean body-weight loss between 7.75% and 9.79% at week 12, while the placebo group saw only a 0.26% reduction. Even those on less frequent dosing—every two weeks or monthly—achieved similar weight loss rates, between 7.86% and 9.73% at week 13, compared to just 0.25% for placebo. These findings suggest that ABBV-295 could offer significant weight loss with flexible dosing schedules.
00:01:29
The early success of ABBV-295 stands out, especially when compared to other amylin analogues in development. For example, Roche recently reported mid-stage data for its own candidate, licensed from Zealand Pharma, in a much larger trial. While each company’s approach and results differ, the competition is heating up. Notably, Gubra had previously shared six-week data showing a 7.77% mean weight loss in the ABBV-295 group versus a weight gain in the placebo group. AbbVie plans to present the full Phase I data at an upcoming scientific conference, which will provide more insight into the drug’s potential. As the race for effective, convenient weight-loss treatments continues, ABBV-295’s early data suggests it could become a key player in the field.

title: Tackling pulmonary fibrosis: Boehringer Ingelheim’s new drug + AI approach
description:
In this episode we sit down with Martin Beck, Senior Vice President and Head of the Inflammation Business Unit at Boehringer Ingelheim (https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/fr) . Martin grew up just down the road from the company’s headquarters in Germany, joined as a scholarship student more than 20 years ago, and never really left – and you’ll hear why he still loves it.


We spend most of the episode focused on a disease that doesn’t get nearly enough attention: idiopathic and progressive pulmonary fibrosis (https://patient.boehringer-ingelheim.com/lwpf/) . These are rare, fatal lung-scarring conditions that kill faster than many cancers, yet patients often shrug off the first symptoms as “just aging.” 


Martin walks us through why half the people on today’s treatments stop taking them, how BI just brought the first new medicine in over a decade to the U.S. market, and why an AI tool that spots microscopic changes on lung scans might finally help doctors diagnose and treat these patients’ years earlier.

description:
不論係面對高齡備孕嘅時間壓力，定係正準備進入 IVF 試管嬰兒療程，好多準媽媽都面臨同一個難題：點樣提升卵子質量同子宮內膜嘅迎受性（Receptivity）？

其實，真正有效嘅輔助方案，背後有一套嚴格嘅「細胞生物學教科書原理」！卵子作為人體內線粒體（Mitochondria）密度最高嘅細胞，其能量儲備直接決定了解凍、受精同分裂嘅成功率。

點解美國專業品牌 Med Glow LED 嘅生殖科學研究技術備受關注？今集我哋用最嚴謹嘅醫學圖解，同你逐層剝開紅光療法（Red Light Therapy）如何進行細胞級助孕：

🔬 生殖醫學級三大核心機制（由細胞層次直達子宮結果）：
1️⃣ 線粒體 ATP 生產 🔋：精準紅光穿透並作用於細胞線粒體，大幅提升內源性 ATP（細胞能量貨幣）生成，直接幫卵子「充電」，延緩細胞老化。
2️⃣ 改善子宮內膜血流 (Post-RLT) 🩸：促進局部微循環與一氧化氮釋放，擴張血管，增加子宮內膜嘅血氧供應與營養輸送。
3️⃣ 優化生殖環境以提高著床率 👶：透過優化子宮內環境與內膜厚度，為受精卵著床創造最佳條件，大大增加成功受孕機會。

Med Glow 拒絕概念炒作，將科學實證嘅專業生殖技術帶入屋企。喺漫長、焦慮嘅備孕路上，你絕對唔會孤單，等我哋用純物理、安全無創嘅光生物調節技術，陪你為新生命準備最溫暖嘅床。

HSG Test म्हणजे काय? | Fallopian Tube Test Guide | Penguin Hospital, Pune

जर तुम्ही pregnancy साठी try करत असाल आणि काही महिन्यांनंतरही conception होत नसेल, तर gynecologist तुम्हाला HSG test (Hysterosalpingography) suggest करू शकतात. ही test fallopian tubes open आहेत की blocked आहेत हे check करण्यासाठी केली जाते. Fallopian tubes या uterus च्या दोन्ही बाजूंना असतात आणि egg ला ovary पासून uterus पर्यंत पोहोचण्यासाठी मदत करतात.

जर tubes blocked असतील, तर egg आणि sperm ची भेट होण्यात problem येऊ शकतो आणि त्यामुळे natural pregnancy conceive होण्यात अडचण येऊ शकते. HSG test मध्ये एक special dye वापरून tubes मध्ये blockage आहे का हे पाहिलं जातं. कारण या tubes खूप thin असतात आणि ultrasound मध्ये clearly दिसत नाहीत.

ही test fertility treatment planning मधील एक important step आहे आणि infertility चं कारण समजून घेण्यासाठी खूप useful ठरते.

title: Hacia la curación de la psoriasis, novedades en investigación con el Dr. Pablo Coto, dermatólogo
description:
El Dr. Pablo Coto Segura, dermatólogo y experto en psoriasis, comparte en esta entrevista sus reflexiones sobre los avances terapéuticos en la enfermedad. Lejos de centrarse en las novedades de la industria farmacéutica, el Dr. Coto propone una mirada renovada hacia la psoriasis, enfatizando la importancia de comprender la enfermedad desde su origen en la piel.

En su intervención, el Dr. Coto destaca el papel fundamental de los queratocitos, las células de la epidermis, tanto en el inicio como en el mantenimiento de la psoriasis. Señala que, si bien los tratamientos actuales han logrado controlar la enfermedad y mejorar la calidad de vida de los pacientes, no han alcanzado la curación. Para lograr este objetivo, el Dr. Coto aboga por “desmontar el castillo” de la inflamación, en lugar de simplemente “vaciándolo” de inquilinos.

La conversación también aborda la microbiota, tanto cutánea como intestinal, como un área prometedora para la investigación y el tratamiento de la psoriasis. El Dr. Coto subraya la necesidad de abordar este campo con seriedad científica, a pesar de su popularidad mediática. Se presentan ejemplos de cómo la modulación de la microbiota ha mostrado resultados sorprendentes en otras enfermedades, como el melanoma metastásico, sugiriendo su potencial en la psoriasis.

El Dr. Coto cierra lanzando un mensaje de esperanza y exigencia a la comunidad científica: la curación de la psoriasis es un objetivo alcanzable si se enfocan los esfuerzos en comprender y abordar las causas subyacentes de la enfermedad. La entrevista concluye con un llamado a seguir investigando y a cambiar la mirada sobre la psoriasis, buscando activamente la curación para los pacientes.

00:00 La Psoriasis: ¿Enfermedad Sistémica o de la Piel?
El Dr. Coto discute si la psoriasis es una enfermedad sistémica o local de la piel. Propone una nueva perspectiva que se enfoca en el queratinocito y su papel en el inicio y mantenimiento de la inflamación.

03:19 ¿Hemos Olvidado al Queratinocito?
El Dr. Coto explica que se ha puesto demasiado énfasis en el sistema inmune, descuidando el papel del queratinocito en el origen de la psoriasis. Argumenta que la piel y lo que sucede en ella es fundamental.

06:48 El Queratinocito y el ‘Castillo Inflamatorio’
El Dr. Coto aclara qué es un queratinocito y su función en la piel. Explica cómo una alteración en estas células puede iniciar una cascada inflamatoria, formando un ‘castillo’ que es el foco de la enfermedad.

10:04 Derribar el Castillo: Hacia la Curación
El doctor utiliza la metáfora del castillo para ilustrar que los tratamientos actuales solo ‘vacían’ la inflamación. Argumenta que la curación de la psoriasis requiere ‘derribar’ el castillo, atacando la raíz del problema en el queratinocito.

13:41 ¿Es Posible la Curación de la Psoriasis?
El Dr. Coto reflexiona sobre la posibilidad de curar la psoriasis. Aunque las herramientas actuales no lo permiten, cree que el conocimiento existente y el desarrollo de nuevas herramientas podrían llevar a la curación.

16:12 La Microbiota: Un Nuevo Enfoque
El Dr. Coto introduce el papel de la microbiota en la psoriasis, tanto cutánea como intestinal. Menciona que las alteraciones en la microbiota pueden influir en la inflamación y las comorbilidades, sugiriendo la modulación de la microbiota como un área de investigación prometedora.

21:20 Consejos para Pacientes y el Futuro de la Psoriasis
El Dr. Coto ofrece consejos a los pacientes, enfatizando la importancia de una dieta sana y evitando el abuso de antibióticos para mantener una microbiota saludable. Reitera la necesidad de buscar la curación y cambiar la perspectiva de la enfermedad.

24:55 Despedida y Agradecimientos
El entrevistador agradece al Dr. Coto por su claridad y franqueza, animando a los pacientes a escuchar su perspectiva. Se cierra la entrevista con la esperanza de que la investigación continúe hacia la curación de la psoriasis.

title: Why hydration matters
description:
Why is hydration important during perimenopause and menopause?

Water plays a major role in temperature regulation, energy levels, and overall body balance.

During hot flashes and night sweats, the body loses fluids through sweating. If hydration drops too low, symptoms like fatigue, dizziness, overheating, or discomfort may feel stronger.

Staying hydrated supports the body’s cooling system and helps maintain normal body functions.

It may seem simple, but water intake can make a difference in how the body feels during hormonal changes.

Sleep is when the body recovers, restores balance, and regulates important systems like stress responses and temperature control.

Why do hot flashes feel completely different from person to person?

Because every body responds differently to hormonal changes.

Some women experience mild warmth for a few seconds, while others feel intense heat, sweating, chills, or a racing heartbeat.

description:
**Minoxidil** is one of the most widely used and scientifically proven treatments for hair loss. Originally developed as an oral medication for high blood pressure, researchers noticed a unique side effect: unexpected hair growth. Today, it is primarily used as a topical solution or foam applied directly to the scalp.
Here are the primary benefits of Minoxidil:
## 1. Stimulates Hair Growth
Minoxidil acts as a **vasodilator**, meaning it widens the blood vessels in the scalp.
 * **More Nutrients:** This increased blood flow delivers more oxygen and essential nutrients directly to the hair follicles.
 * **Follicle Revitalization:** It reactivates shrunken or dormant hair follicles, encouraging them to start producing hair again.
## 2. Prolongs the Anagen (Growth) Phase
Hair grows in cycles: growth (anagen), resting (catagen), and shedding (telogen). Minoxidil extends the duration of the **anagen phase**. This allows individual hair strands to grow for a longer period before falling out, leading to longer and thicker hair over time.
## 3. Reverses Hair Thinning
Minoxidil increases the physical size and thickness of the hair follicles. This process reverses "miniaturization" (where hair follicles shrink and producker, denser, and more robust hair strands**.
## 4. Treats Multiple Types of Hair Loss
While most famous for treating hereditary hair loss, it is effective for a few different conditions:
 * **Androgenetic Alopecia:** The most common use case (Male Pattern Baldness and Female tern Hair Loss).

Genau darum geht es in diesem Gespräch mit Jasmin Meißl. Jasmin ist Human Design Analytikerin und hat 35 Jahre lang mehrere Kindergärten geleitet. Sie kennt Kinder wie kaum jemand sonst. title: Webinar for Stroke Survivors: Women's Health - Menopause After Stroke
description:
What happens when menopause and stroke recovery intersect? In this honest and informative Different Strokes webinar, stroke survivors and healthcare professionals come together to discuss an important topic that is too often overlooked: menopause after stroke.

Hosted by Different Strokes, this free webinar explores the physical, emotional and practical challenges women may experience during menopause following a stroke. Our panel shares personal experiences, advice and reflections to help stroke survivors feel more informed, supported and less alone.

In this webinar, we hear from:

• Dr Satinder Sanghera, GP, stroke survivor and Different Strokes trustee
• Genise, stroke survivor and Family Support Officer at Different Strokes

Together, they discuss:

• Symptoms of menopause after stroke
• HRT and medical advice after stroke
• Fatigue, brain fog and emotional changes
• Confidence, identity and wellbeing
• The lack of information available for younger stroke survivors
• Why open conversations and peer support matter

At Different Strokes, we know that stroke recovery is different for everyone. By sharing real experiences and expert insight, we hope this webinar helps raise awareness and support more women navigating menopause after stroke.

Different Strokes is a UK charity supporting younger stroke survivors and their families through peer support, information, exercise and community.

Find out more about Different Strokes and our support services:

title: भारत की सबसे बड़ी विदेशी डील: Sun Pharma to Acquire Organon for $13 Billion #sunpharma #breakingnews
description:
🚨 भारत की फार्मा इंडस्ट्री का सबसे बड़ा दिन! Big Breaking News 🚨

28 अप्रैल 2026 को Dainik Bhaskar में छपी खबर के अनुसार, भारत की No.1 दवा कंपनी Sun Pharmaceutical Industries ने अमेरिका की दिग्गज फार्मा कंपनी Organon को 1.10 लाख करोड़ रुपये में खरीदने का ऐलान किया है। 

This is the BIGGEST ever overseas acquisition by any Indian pharmaceutical company. Cash deal के साथ Sun Pharma अब सीधे Pfizer, Novartis और Johnson & Johnson की league में खेलने जा रही है।

📊 Deal की पूरी Details:
• Deal Value: ₹1,10,000 करोड़ | $13.2 Billion Approx • Share Price: $14 per share पर Organon के सभी शेयर खरीदेगी Sun Pharma • Timeline: 2027 तक पूरा सौदा नकद में होगा • Organon Revenue: ₹58,000 करोड़ सालाना राजस्व वाली कंपनी • Debt Included: Organon का ₹81,000 करोड़ का कर्ज भी Sun Pharma लेगी • Combined Revenue: डील के बाद संयुक्त राजस्व ₹1.16 लाख करोड़ होगा 
🌍 इस डील से क्या होगा?
1. Global Ranking: Sun Pharma दुनिया की Top-25 दवा कंपनियों में शामिल हो जाएगी 2. Global Reach: 100+ देशों से बढ़कर 150+ देशों में पहुंच 3. Biosimilars: दुनिया की 7वीं सबसे बड़ी biosimilar दवाओं वाली कंपनी बनेगी 4. Market Access: US और Europe के 18 बड़े बाजारों में सीधी एंट्री 5. Employees: Organon के 10,000 कर्मचारी भी Sun Pharma का हिस्सा बनेंगे 
💡 Sun Pharma का सफर - 10 हजार से 4 लाख करोड़ तक
1983: दिलीप सांघवी ने पिता से ₹10,000 उधार लेकर 5 दोस्तों के साथ 1 कमरे में कंपनी शुरू की
1993: Schizophrenia की दवा Clozapine लॉन्च की
2014: Ranbaxy का अधिग्रहण करके भारत की No.1 कंपनी बनी
2025: Checkpoint Therapeutics का अधिग्रहण 
2026: Organon Deal - अब Global Top-25 में एंट्री

आज Sun Pharma की Market Cap ₹4 लाख करोड़ है. दुनिया की सबसे बड़ी generic दवा बनाने वाली कंपनियों में से एक है. 41 manufacturing units, 2 हजार से ज्यादा products.

🇮🇳 भारत के लिए क्यों गर्व की बात है?
America के generic बाजार में 40% दवाइयां भारत से जाती हैं. Europe में 25% share है. अब Indian कंपनियां सिर्फ दवा बेच नहीं रहीं, बल्कि US-Europe की कंपनियों को खरीद भी रही हैं. 

Expert मैत्री सेठ के अनुसार, "इस डील से Sun Pharma अब Pfizer जैसी innovator कंपनी की league में आ जाएगी."

📈 Stock Market Impact:
Deal announce होने के बाद Sun Pharma के शेयर 7% से 9% तक चढ़ गए. कंपनी का कहना है कि इस डील से innovative और specialty drugs में भी भारत एक वैश्विक शक्ति बन सकता है.

title: Tariff Impact, Cash Flows & The Reason Behind Buying Organon: Sun Pharma Management Answers It All
description:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. shares jumped over 5% during early trade on Monday after it announced the acquisition of New York-listed Organon & Co. in an all‑cash transaction with an enterprise valuation of $11.75 billion. The Indian drugmaker will buy all outstanding shares for $14 per share in cash, or approximately $3.99 billion in total equity value, according to a stock exchange filing. "The proposed acquisition of Organon is aligned with Sun Pharma's strategy of growing its Innovative Medicines business. The combined company becomes a stronger player in Established Brands/Branded Generics business. Organon's portfolio, global footprint and strong stakeholder relationships shall complement Sun Pharma's existing strengths and enhance long‑term value creation," a statement said. The acquisition is expected to be completed in early 2027, subject to customary conditions, including regulatory approvals and Organon stockholder approval. Sun Pharma plans to fund the acquisition through a combination of available cash resources ($2-2.5 billion) and committed financing from banks ($9.25-9.75 billion) including Citigroup Global Markets Asia Ltd., JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. and MUFG Bank Ltd.

description: POV: You Have a Birth Control Ring. Sources- PMID 21151688 callmeddy. on TT The birth control ring is a flexible, plastic insert that provides a continuous and consistent dose of both estrogen and progesterone directly through the vaginal lining into the bloodstream. Unlike the oral contraceptive pill, which creates a daily "peak and valley" of hormone levels after each ingestion, the ring sits in place for three weeks and releases a steady, low-dose stream of medication. This bypasses the digestive system and ensures that the body maintains a stable hormonal environment, which effectively suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus to block sperm, and thins the uterine lining to prevent implantation. Because the hormones are absorbed locally, the ring can often maintain high efficacy with a lower overall systemic dose compared to some other methods. For many users, a major benefit of the ring is its flexibility and the fact that it does not require a daily "memory task." While the ring is designed to stay in place during exercise, swimming, and sexual intercourse, some individuals find it uncomfortable during certain activities. If the ring is causing physical discomfort or becomes displaced, it can be safely removed for up to 3 hours within any 24-hour period without compromising its contraceptive effectiveness. It is important to rinse the ring with cool or lukewarm water (never hot) before reinserting it to ensure it remains clean. title: What is the birth control patch? The patch is a birth control method that sticks to your skin like a
description: What is the birth control patch? The patch is a birth control method that sticks to your skin like a small Band-Aid It contains two different kinds of hormones, estrogen and progestin, that work together to prevent pregnancy. These hormones are absorbed through your skin. The main way they prevent pregnancy is by stopping ovulation from happening, which means that your ovaries don’t release an egg. The patch is very effective the way most people use it. Typical use: 93% effective The patch is simple to use: all you have to do is take off your old patch and put on a new one once a week, on the same day of the week, for three weeks in a row. On the day you would normally change your patch at the beginning of the fourth week, you’ll just take off the old one and not put on a new one. Side effects Nausea, irregular bleeding, headaches, and sore breasts are the most common side effects, but they’re usually temporary. title: ✨ Birth Control Spotlight: The Ring ✨ Let’s talk about two ring options: NuvaRing and Annovera
description: ✨ Birth Control Spotlight: The Ring ✨ Let’s talk about two ring options: NuvaRing and Annovera. Both are small, flexible rings that sit inside the v*gina and release hormones (estrogen + progestin) to prevent pregnancy. 💜 How it works: The ring slowly releases hormones into your bloodstream. This prevents your ovaries from releasing an egg, thickens cervical mucus (harder for sp-rm to swim through), and thins the uterine lining. 💡 NuvaRing vs. Annovera: 🔹 NuvaRing: Insert for 3 weeks, remove for 1 week (for your period*), then replace with a new one. 🔹 Annovera: One reusable ring lasts an entire year! Insert for 3 weeks, remove for 1 week, then reinsert the same ring. 📈 Effectiveness: About 91 - 93% effective with typical use. ✨ Pros: * No daily pill to remember 🙌 * Can help make periods lighter + more predictable * Private, most people won’t know you’re using it * Annovera can be kept at room temp (travel-friendly!) ⚠️ Cons / Things to consider: * Requires comfort with placing something inside your v*gina (you insert it yourself) * May cause spotting, br-ast tenderness, or mood changes * Not recommended if you have certain health conditions (like a history of blood clots) * Some people feel it during s-x (you or your partner may notice, most don’t) 👩🏽‍⚕️ Dr. J’s tip: If you’re forgetful about daily pills but not ready to commit to a longer-term method like an IUD or implant, the ring can be a great middle ground. Annovera especially is low-maintenance …. set it, forget it, reuse it! 💬 Would you be comfortable inserting the ring yourself, or would that feel like a dealbreaker? Drop your thoughts ⬇️ 🟣 Reminder: There’s no “one size fits all” birth control. “Tiny Implant = No Pregnancy?”#birthcontrol#contraceptiveimplant #medicine #health 


“This tiny device is called a contraceptive implant, also known as Nexplanon. It’s a small flexible rod placed under the skin of the upper arm by a doctor. The implant slowly releases a hormone called progestin that prevents ovulation, thickens cervical mucus, and makes pregnancy extremely unlikely. It can work for up to 3 to 5 years depending on the version used. The procedure takes only a few minutes and is reversible, meaning it can be removed anytime. Some people may experience side effects like irregular periods, headaches, or acne, so medical consultation is important before using it.”

title: “My Arm Implant is Lost” #how
description:
Sources- PMID 38712717 
barbz.creates on TT 

The contraceptive arm implant, a small flexible rod often known by the brand name Nexplanon, is designed to stay in the subdermal tissue of the inner upper arm for several years. While rare, a complication known as migration can occur, where the implant moves from its original insertion site. Most cases of migration are localized, meaning the rod shifts only an inch or two within the arm tissue. This usually happens if the implant was placed too deeply during the initial procedure or if vigorous physical activity or trauma to the arm occurs shortly after insertion before the surrounding tissue has had time to "anchor" the device in place. A much rarer but more serious form of migration involves the implant entering the vascular system. If the rod is accidentally inserted into a vein or if it erodes through a vessel wall, it can travel through the bloodstream to other parts of the body. In these highly unusual cases, the implant can be carried to the pulmonary artery in the lungs. While this sounds alarming, many "lost" implants are located using specialized imaging like X-rays or ultrasound and can often be removed via a minimally invasive endovascular procedure.

title: Implant (Nexplanon) Removal: What to Expect Before, During, and After
description:
Video Credit: IG@babymommadoc_

Nexplanon is a small, flexible contraceptive implant inserted under the skin of the upper arm. It releases a hormone called etonogestrel to prevent pregnancy and is effective for up to three years. When it reaches the end of its lifespan—or earlier if needed—it must be removed by a trained healthcare professional. Understanding the removal process can help ease anxiety and prepare individuals for what to expect.

Why Nexplanon May Need to Be Removed

There are several reasons why someone may choose or need to have their Nexplanon implant removed. The most common reason is that it has reached the end of its three-year effectiveness. Others may wish to remove it earlier due to side effects such as irregular bleeding, headaches, mood changes, weight changes, acne, or reduced libido. Some people request removal because they want to become pregnant, while others may switch to a different method of contraception or have medical reasons that make continued use unsuitable.

When Can Nexplanon Be Removed?

Nexplanon can be removed at any time, not just at the three-year mark. Fertility can return very quickly after removal, sometimes within days, so it is important to consider alternative contraception if pregnancy is not desired. In some cases, a new Nexplanon implant can be inserted immediately after removal during the same appointment.

How the Removal Procedure Is Done

The removal of Nexplanon is a minor outpatient procedure that usually takes only a few minutes. The healthcare provider will first locate the implant by feeling under the skin. The area is then cleaned and numbed with a local anaesthetic. A small incision is made near the tip of the implant, and gentle pressure is applied to push the implant out. It is then grasped with forceps and removed. Once removed, the incision is closed with steri-strips or a small dressing, and a pressure bandage may be applied.

Does Removal Hurt?

Most people feel little to no pain during the procedure because of the local anaesthetic. Some pressure or tugging may be felt, but this is usually mild. After the procedure, the area may feel tender or bruised for a few days, which is normal.

Aftercare and Recovery

After Nexplanon removal, it is advised to keep the pressure bandage on for 24 hours and the smaller dressing in place for a few days. The arm should be kept clean and dry, and strenuous activity involving that arm should be avoided for a short period. Mild bruising, swelling, or soreness can occur but typically resolves on its own. Signs of infection such as increasing redness, severe pain, pus, or fever should be reported to a healthcare provider promptly.

What Happens After Removal?

Once Nexplanon is removed, the hormone levels in the body fall quickly. Menstrual cycles may return to their previous pattern, although this can take a few weeks or months for some individuals. Fertility returns rapidly, so pregnancy is possible soon after removal. If contraception is still needed, another method should be started immediately.

Possible Complications

Complications from Nexplanon removal are uncommon but can include infection, scarring, or difficulty removing the implant if it is deeply placed or not easily felt. In rare cases, imaging such as ultrasound may be needed to locate the implant before removal.

Key Takeaway

Nexplanon removal is a simple and safe procedure when performed by a trained professional. Whether removal is due to side effects, a desire to conceive, or routine replacement, understanding the process can help reduce fear and ensure a smooth experience. Anyone considering removal should discuss their options and future contraceptive plans with a healthcare provider.

title: Birth Control Implant (Nexplanon) | Benefits, Side Effects & Procedure Explained #Health&Sehath
description:
#BirthControlImplant(Nexplanon)| Benefits,SideEffects&Procedure/Explained

Today’s video is a complete, detailed guide about the **birth control implant**, also known as **Nexplanon**.

If you are thinking about long-term contraception that is safe, effective, and hormone-based, this video is for you.

So let’s begin.


---


## **🔶 WHAT IS THE BIRTH CONTROL IMPLANT?**


The birth control implant is a **small, flexible rod** about the size of a matchstick.

It is inserted **under the skin of your upper arm** by a trained healthcare professional.

This device releases a hormone called **etonogestrel**, which helps prevent pregnancy.


---


## **🔶 HOW DOES IT WORK?**


The implant prevents pregnancy in **three main ways**:


1. **Stops ovulation**

   Your ovaries stop releasing an egg each month.


2. **Thickens cervical mucus**

   This makes it very hard for sperm to reach the egg.


3. **Thins the lining of the uterus**

   So even if an egg is released, it cannot implant.




---


## **🔶 EFFECTIVENESS**


* The implant is **99% effective**.

* It works for **3 years** continuously.

* No daily pill, no injections, no remembering dates.


This is why many women prefer it for long-term protection.


---


## **🔶 WHO CAN USE IT?**


The implant is suitable for:


✔ Married women

✔ Mothers who don’t want pregnancy for a few years

✔ Women who want a hormone method without daily pills

✔ Breastfeeding mothers (safe after 6 weeks)

✔ Women with heavy periods

✔ Women who forget pills


---


## **🔶 WHO SHOULD AVOID IT?**




✘You have breast cancer

✘ You have severe liver disease

✘ You are pregnant 

✘ You have unexplained vaginal bleeding


Always consult a doctor before getting it inserted.


---


## **🔶 BENEFITS OF THE IMPLANT**


The implant has several advantages:


### **1. Long-lasting protection**


One insert works for **3 years**.


### **2. High effectiveness**


More reliable than pills and injections.


### **3. No maintenance**


Once inserted, you don’t need to do anything.


### **4. Lighter periods**


Many women experience lighter bleeding or even no periods.


### **5. Safe during breastfeeding**


Does not affect milk supply.


### **6. Quick return of fertility**


Once removed, you can get pregnant soon.


---


## **🔶 POSSIBLE SIDE EFFECTS**


Like any hormonal method, the implant may cause:


* Irregular periods

* Lighter or heavier bleeding

* Headache

* Mood changes

* Breast tenderness

* Weight changes in some women

* Spotting

* Arm soreness after insertion


These side effects usually improve with time.


---


## **🔶 INSERTION PROCEDURE (STEP-BY-STEP)**


1. You visit a clinic.

2. Your arm is cleaned and numbed with local anesthesia.

3. The implant is inserted under the skin using a small device.

4. The procedure takes **only 2–3 minutes**.

5. A small bandage is applied.

6. You can go home immediately.


**It does NOT need stitches.**

**It is almost painless due to the numbing injection.**


---


## **🔶 REMOVAL PROCEDURE**


* Takes about **5 minutes**.

* A tiny cut is made to slide the implant out.

* You can insert a new one the same day if you want. ?


---


## **🔶 MYTHS VS REALITY**


**Myth 1:** The implant moves inside the body.

**Reality:** It stays exactly where it is inserted.


**Myth 2:** It causes infertility.

**Reality:** Fertility returns quickly after removal.


**Myth 3:** It is very painful.

**Reality:** Only mild discomfort due to anesthesia.


---


## **🔶 SAFETY**


The implant is considered **one of the safest contraceptive methods**, approved by:


✔ WHO

✔ FDA

✔ Gynecologists worldwide

title: “Coloquei o DIU Mirena… mas continuo com dores, escapes e desconforto. E agora?”
description:
“Coloquei o DIU Mirena… mas continuo com dores, escapes e desconforto. E agora?”

Essa é uma dúvida muito mais comum do que parece. 💛
Muitas mulheres passam anos convivendo com dores pélvicas intensas sem entender a verdadeira origem do problema — e só recebem o diagnóstico correto após exames mais específicos, como a ultrassonografia com preparo intestinal.

A adenomiose difusa é uma condição inflamatória do útero que pode provocar sintomas extremamente limitantes:
🔹 Cólicas fortes
🔹 Dor pélvica crônica
🔹 Sensação de peso abdominal
🔹 Sangramentos prolongados
🔹 Escapes frequentes
🔹 Dor nas relações
🔹 Impacto emocional e desgaste constante

O DIU hormonal, como o Mirena, pode sim ajudar muitas pacientes porque reduz o estímulo hormonal sobre o endométrio e costuma diminuir sangramento e dor. Porém, nem todas as mulheres conseguem adaptação adequada ao método.

Quando a paciente continua apresentando dores importantes, escapes persistentes, sensação de ardência ou desconforto contínuo, é fundamental reavaliar cuidadosamente:
✔️ a intensidade da adenomiose
✔️ possível associação com endometriose
✔️ posicionamento do DIU
✔️ outras causas ginecológicas e inflamatórias
✔️ qualidade de vida da paciente

E existe um ponto muito importante: tratamento não deve ser apenas “tolerar sintomas”. O objetivo é devolver funcionalidade, conforto e qualidade de vida. ✨

Cada caso precisa ser individualizado. Algumas pacientes melhoram muito com tratamento hormonal; outras necessitam mudança de estratégia terapêutica, acompanhamento especializado ou até abordagem cirúrgica, dependendo da gravidade e dos objetivos da mulher.

Por isso, ouvir o corpo e validar o próprio sofrimento faz parte do processo de cuidado. Dor constante nunca deve ser normalizada.

title: Should you use the mirena IUD in perimenopause?
description:
Noooooo girl nooooo 😩⁠
⁠
Honestly, I can’t believe drs are still saying this / recommending this in 2025. ⁠
⁠
It’s one thing to go on the hormonal IUD for contraception because it’s highly effective. ⁠
⁠
But it’s another thing to use it as symptom management without looking at the underlying causes of those symptoms.⁠
⁠
And it *certainly* does not support your progesterone because (broken record over here):⁠
⁠
Progesterone and progestin (the synthetic hormone in the Mirena) are NOT the same. ⁠
⁠
Scroll back to my recent post comparing the 2 if you want to learn more!⁠
⁠
- In a nut shell, progesterone provides health benefits like soothing the nervous system and supporting your bones, while progestin (especially Levonorgestrel, which is what’s in the Mirena) comes along with health risks like increased depression risk and a whole lot more). ⁠
⁠
Also, so many women are being told to go on or stay on the Mirena through perimenopause until they reach menopause (for symptom management), but why wouldn’t we recommend actual progesterone to address symptoms instead???⁠
⁠
Let me know your questions in the comments 👇🏽⁠
⁠
Here's my free guide, the Low Progesterone Fix:
https://fixyourperiod.com/low-progesterone-opt-in/

title: Mirena IUD Show and Tell!#womenshealth #birthcontrol #perimenopause #iud #hormonetherapy
description:
Not an Ad, just a great option to consider.
If heavy periods have been stealing your peace lately, you’re not alone 🌊
Perimenopause can turn already heavy cycles into something truly exhausting — and that’s worth talking about. But here’s something that often flies under the radar: heavy or frequent periods can quietly drain your iron stores, leading to iron deficiency or even anaemia. 🩸
Feeling extra tired, foggy, breathless, or just off? Your heavy flow might be taking more from you than you realize. Iron deficiency from heavy menses is more common than most people think — and it’s absolutely worth checking with your doctor.
The Mirena IUD is a small, hormone-releasing device that many people (myself included ✋) find life-changing during this season of life. It works locally in the uterus to significantly lighten (and sometimes stop) periods, without the full-body effects of systemic hormones. 💛
Here’s what makes it worth knowing about:
✨ Can reduce heavy bleeding by up to 90%
✨ Works for up to 8 years (*5 if used specifically in combined menopause hormone therapy)
✨ Provides contraception during the perimenopause transition
✨ May ease cramping too
✨ Lightening your flow can help protect your iron levels
Your body is going through a lot right now — and you deserve to feel like yourself again. If heavy bleeding is affecting your quality of life, this is your reminder that it doesn’t have to be your new normal. Talk to your provider about whether a hormonal IUD might be right for you 🩷
Always advocate for yourself. You’ve got this. 💪

title: Mirena-IUD #mbbs #mbbsmotivation #mbbsstudent #mbbslife #gynecology #obgyn #contraceptives
description:
Mirena is a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device (LNG-IUS) used for long-term reversible contraception and several gynecological indications. It releases 20 µg/day of levonorgestrel, causing endometrial suppression, thick cervical mucus, and inhibition of sperm motility, which prevents fertilization.

🔹 Type: Hormonal intrauterine device (IUD)
🔹 Hormone: Levonorgestrel (progesterone)
🔹 Duration of Action: Up to 5–8 years (depending on guideline updates)
🔹 Mechanism: Endometrial atrophy + thick cervical mucus + impaired sperm transport
🔹 Contraceptive Failure Rate: ~ less than 1% (very high efficacy)

Clinical Uses:
• Long-term contraception
• Treatment of heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia)
• Protection of endometrium during estrogen therapy
• Sometimes used in adenomyosis and endometriosis

Advantages:
✔ Highly effective reversible contraception
✔ Reduced menstrual bleeding and dysmenorrhea
✔ Low systemic hormone exposure
✔ Long duration with a single insertion

Common Side Effects:
• Irregular bleeding/spotting (initial months)
• Amenorrhea over time
• Breast tenderness
• Mood changes

Contraindications:
❌ Pregnancy
❌ Active pelvic infection / PID
❌ Unexplained uterine bleeding
❌ Uterine anomalies distorting cavity

💡 Exam Tip for MBBS/NEET-PG: Mirena primarily works by local progesterone effect on the endometrium, not by suppressing ovulation in most cycles.

title: Heavy Periods: How Mirena Replaced Unnecessary Hysterectomy
description:
If heavy menstrual bleeding is controlling your life, or your doctor has mentioned Mirena as a treatment option, this video breaks down everything you genuinely need to know. 🎯
Mirena is a small, soft hormonal IUS (intrauterine system) that sits inside the uterus and releases levonorgestrel, a lab-made form of progesterone, directly to the uterine lining. Unlike oral tablets that travel through the liver, heart, and ten other organs before reaching their target, Mirena delivers hormones locally, at just 1/750th the dose of oral medication. That is why the side effect profile is dramatically lower.
Here is what the research says. Mirena succeeds in treating heavy menstrual bleeding in 91 out of 100 women. Within 3 to 12 months, haemoglobin levels rise, meaning more energy, better focus, and real quality of life improvement. 🌿 Studies also show that 64 out of 100 women who use Mirena correctly avoid hysterectomy altogether.
Beyond heavy periods, Mirena has proven benefits in endometriosis, adenomyosis, uterine fibroids, and endometrial hyperplasia, a pre-cancer condition of the uterus lining. In fact, Mirena reduces the risk of endometrial cancer through three distinct molecular pathways, offering genuine gynaecological cancer protection that oral progesterone cannot match. For women with PCOS-related uterine lining problems, Mirena is increasingly the recommended approach.
We also cover how Mirena is fitted, whether hysteroscopy is needed, what to expect during those first few months, and how to manage the rare Mirena crash after removal. 💡
If you are exploring non-surgical alternatives to hysterectomy, or want to understand hormonal IUS therapy from a clinical perspective, this is the video for you.

Uzun dönem hormonal tedavilerin izlem gereksinimi göz önüne alındığında, Finasterid kullanımı düzenli hekim takibi ve laboratuvar değerlendirmeleri gerektirir. title: Minoxidil vs. Finasteride: Which Is Better for Hair Loss?
description:
Book an Appointment with Dr. Kopelman: https://calendly.com/drkopelman/
For Surgical Consultations: (212) 831-8333

Minoxidil and Finasteride are two of the most well-known treatments for hair loss, but they work in very different ways. Minoxidil is a topical solution or foam that increases blood flow to the scalp, revitalizing hair follicles and prolonging the growth phase. It’s best for those looking to maintain or slightly improve hair density but does not address the root cause of hair loss.

Finasteride, on the other hand, is an oral medication that blocks the conversion of testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the hormone responsible for genetic hair loss. By reducing DHT levels by about 70%, finasteride effectively slows hair loss and can even promote regrowth in many patients.

Which is better? It depends on your goals. For most men with androgenetic alopecia, finasteride is the stronger option for preventing hair loss, while minoxidil can be a helpful add-on to improve hair density. Many patients benefit from using both together.

description:

Timestamps:
[00:00:14] 🧬 GT20029 protac mechanism targets the androgen receptor
Kintor Pharmaceuticals' GT20029 is a proteolysis targeting chimera that attaches ubiquitin to the androgen receptor on dermal papilla and other follicle cells, marking it for degradation so DHT loses its docking site and cannot transmit the miniaturization signal, with consistent dosing required since the body continuously replenishes fresh receptors

[00:02:11] 🧪 Phase 1 safety data shows minimal systemic exposure
Chinese phase 1 trials showed no detectable drug after single doses and concentrations below 0.05 ng/mL after multiple gel or solution applications, while the US phase 1 trial confirmed concentrations not exceeding 0.015 ng/mL after 14 days of repeated dosing across healthy volunteers and AGA or acne subjects, critical because systemic androgen receptor blockade could otherwise cause libido issues and muscle wasting

[00:07:27] 📊 Phase 2 efficacy results show clinically meaningful hair regrowth
In 180 Chinese men with Norwood 3 to 5 vertex AGA randomized into six arms over 12 weeks, the 0.5% once daily arm beat placebo by 6.69 hairs per cm² and the 1% twice weekly arm beat placebo by 7.36 hairs per cm² with significant hair width improvement, results later published by Hu et al. 2025 in the Journal of Dermatological Treatment

[00:10:54] ⚠️ Dose response inconsistencies and likely explanations
1% once daily did not clearly outperform 0.5% once daily and twice weekly looked more dose responsive than daily dosing, but the 1% daily group started at roughly 105 hairs per cm² versus 119 for its placebo (a 14 hair per cm² baseline disadvantage), and with only 30 per group the small exploratory design plus protac biology requiring time for receptor reset likely explains the inconsistency rather than failed higher dosing

[00:15:43] 🔬 GPR133 pathway as a second DHT damage route
Li et al. 2026 used single cell and spatial transcriptomics to argue DHT also acts through GPR133, driving hyper contractility of the connective tissue sheath via the Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel, which induces apoptosis of follicle progenitor cells and suppresses matrix and outer root sheath proliferation, with GPR133 knockdown producing broader improvements than androgen receptor knockdown which failed to relieve mechanical sheath contraction

[00:21:31] 💊 Implications for anti-androgen strategy versus DHT reduction
Because DHT damages follicles through both the androgen receptor and the GPR133 pathway, topical anti-androgens like pyrilutamide, clascoterone, and RU58841 may leave the GPR-mediated route unaddressed, suggesting 5-alpha reductase inhibitors like finasteride or dutasteride could be more comprehensive by cutting off the substrate feeding both pathways

[00:24:02] 🔍 Methodological limitations of the Li et al. GPR133 study
The strongest mechanistic work was done in isolated human hair follicles in ex vivo organ culture and humanized mouse grafts, stripping away the native follicular niche and dermal papilla signaling context needed to fairly rank GPR133 against the androgen receptor pathway in AGA pathophysiology'

[00:27:07] 🧩 Contradiction with established dermal papilla biology
The paper claims dermal papilla subclusters are broadly comparable between balding and non-balding follicles with only reduced angiogenesis signaling, which conflicts with standard biopsy data showing occipital dermal papillae are larger and more cellularly active than smaller temporal hairline dermal papillae, and even contradicts the same team's earlier paper on AR-mediated paracrine signaling and blood vessel regression

[00:30:30] 📍 Regional and phenotypic variation in hair follicle biology
Overactive GPR133 signaling may be relevant only in specific scalp regions like the hairline or in conditions resembling frontal fibrosing alopecia and DUPA-like phenotypes, while broader AGA biopsy literature 

[00:35:34] 🧬 Testosterone does not activate the GPR133 pathway
A screen of 37 steroid hormones found only DHT and the synthetic androgen methenolone (Primobolan) meaningfully activated GPR133, while testosterone itself did not, reinforcing that conventional DHT-focused treatment strategies remain the rational target

[00:37:10] 💡 Final verdict on GT20029 as a finasteride alternative
GT20029's protac mechanism and supporting clinical signals position it as a meaningful option for patients who cannot tolerate finasteride, do not want to commit to dutasteride, experienced side effects on 5-alpha reductase inhibitors, or want to stack therapies for stronger combined results, since the androgen receptor pathway remains the dominant driver of AGA

title: Why I Stopped Using Finasteride to Fight Hair Loss at 40 (DHT Is Not A Junk Hormone)
description:
Disclaimer: I am not a doctor. I am only sharing my personal experience and research.

Is DHT really just a "junk hormone" that adult men can safely eliminate to save their hair? I heavily disagree. In this video, I share my personal 6-month journey with Finasteride, the side effects I experienced, and why I ultimately chose to prioritize my hormonal health over cosmetic appearance.

DHT is the quintessential male hormone—it is what develops male characteristics in the womb and drives puberty. It is roughly five times stronger than testosterone, and unlike testosterone, it cannot convert into estrogen.

During my time on Finasteride, my doctor accidentally started me on a 5mg prostate-medication dosage instead of the standard 1mg hair loss dose. While I caught the mistake after a week, it completely killed my libido. Even after dropping to 1mg, it became clear to me that this medication is a direct trade-off between cosmetics and overall physical and mental functioning.

The Mental Health Connection & Brain Fog

Many people do not realize that Finasteride crosses the blood-brain barrier. DHT acts as a precursor to critical neurosteroids in the brain that regulate mood, anxiety, and cognitive function. As someone living with manic depression, I found myself far more sensitive to a 90% reduction in my system's DHT, experiencing noticeable brain fog. Individuals with pre-existing mental health issues may experience a much more severe psychological reaction to this hormonal shift.

Overcoming Hair Loss Permanently at 41

Losing hair on top of your head is purely a cosmetic issue. After experiencing a midlife transition at age 40, I had to deal with the underlying vanity and mental hurdles surrounding balding. True internal masculinity isn't about radically modifying your baseline chemistry for a cosmetic result; it's about external influence, confidence, and charisma.

Today, at 41 years old, my hair has actually returned thicker simply by managing my lifestyle. By focusing purely on a low-carb diet and actively reducing my stress levels, I stabilized my hair health without sacrificing the very hormone that makes me a man.

title: Not Minoxidil.  Not Finasteride.  What Is MLPH? #hairloss #shorts
description:
Not minoxidil.
Not finasteride.
So what exactly is MLPH?

MLPH is a new experimental hair loss peptide being studied for a different approach to hair growth. Instead of simply stimulating growth like minoxidil or reducing DHT like finasteride and dutasteride, MLPH is designed to activate signaling in dermal papilla cells — the “command center” cells that help regulate hair follicle behavior.

In simple terms, this may represent a more follicle-targeted approach to hair loss treatment.

But important note: MLPH is still experimental and not yet an approved treatment. More human clinical studies are needed to confirm its safety and effectiveness.

description:
Entender se você precisa de transplante capilar ou se ainda pode tratar a calvície com minoxidil e finasterida é essencial para um resultado eficaz.

title: Почему почти все звезды сидят на финастериде: Трамп, Эштон Катчер и еще тысячи мужчин
description:
Препарат на котором сидит весь Голливуд

Косметика для волос https://t.me/healthyhair_shop
Телеграм: https://t.me/volosasha

Если ты думаешь, что только ты боишься финастерида — ты не один. Через этот страх проходят почти все мужчины, которые начинают лысеть. Я тоже через это проходил. Я читал форумы, истории про «убитое либидо», импотенцию, депрессию, необратимые побочки. Казалось, что одна таблетка может сломать жизнь.

Но потом я начал глубже копать тему. И понял одну вещь: количество людей, которые принимают финастерид, просто огромное. Намного больше, чем кажется. Cамое забавное — многие из них известные люди.

Например, Дональд Трамп открыто говорил, что принимает Propecia. Да, президент США, один из самых влиятельных людей в мире, использовал препарат от выпадения волос.

Стив Каррелл — человек, которого многие знают по сериалу «Офис». Даже в самом сериале тема Propecia мелькала как что-то абсолютно обычное.

Эштон Катчер рассказывал, что принимал дутастерид — еще более мощный препарат, чем финастерид. А это актер, которого многие считают буквально эталоном мужской внешности.
Дак Шепард. Роб Лоу. И это только те, кто признавался публично.

Даже Ян Топлес в интервью рассказывал про блокировку ДГТ и таблетки от выпадения волос. И в какой-то момент ты начинаешь понимать: огромное количество людей вокруг либо сидят на финастериде, либо хотя бы знают о нем намного больше, чем делают вид.

Проблема в другом. Вокруг финастерида слишком много мифов.
Мужчинам после 30 и без того становится сложнее: стресс, плохой сон, алкоголь, сигареты, отсутствие спорта, лишний вес, проблемы с сосудами, тревожность. Но когда начинается облысение и человек параллельно начинает пить финастерид — очень легко назначить виноватым именно таблетку. Хотя зачастую проблема вообще не в ней.

Я, например, в один период одновременно принимал антидепрессанты, финастерид, таблетки от холестерина и при этом еще курил. И никаких проблем с либидо или эрекцией у меня не было.

Это не значит, что побочек не существует. Они возможны. Но интернет создает ощущение, будто они происходят у всех подряд. Хотя в исследованиях серьезные побочные эффекты встречаются редко. Самое главное — сегодня уже есть не только классический финастерид.

Есть топические формы — когда препарат наносится на кожу головы. Они намного меньше попадают в кровоток. Есть новые антиандрогены вроде KX-826 и RU58841, которые работают вообще по другому принципу.

Но реальность остается реальностью: большинство мужчин, которые смогли сохранить волосы, скорее всего используют антиандрогенную терапию. Особенно после пересадки.
Потому что пересадка без блокировки ДГТ — это очень часто временная история. Ты пересаживаешь волосы, а через несколько лет продолжаешь терять свои родные.

Поэтому главный вопрос не в том, страшный ли финастерид.
Главный вопрос — что для тебя хуже: рискнуть и сохранить волосы… или ничего не делать и гарантированно продолжить лысеть.

description:

Montelukast 10 mg es un medicamento utilizado para tratar diferentes condiciones respiratorias, principalmente el asma y la rinitis alérgica. Pertenece a una clase de fármacos conocidos como antagonistas de los receptores de leucotrienos. Los leucotrienos son sustancias químicas en el cuerpo que desempeñan un papel importante en la inflamación y la respuesta alérgica.

Su principal función es bloquear la acción de los leucotrienos, lo que ayuda a reducir la inflamación en las vías respiratorias, relajar los músculos bronquiales y mejorar los síntomas asociados con el asma y la rinitis alérgica.

En el caso del asma, Montelukast 10 mg se utiliza tanto para el tratamiento crónico como para la prevención de los ataques agudos de asma en adultos y niños mayores de 6 años. Ayuda a reducir la frecuencia y la gravedad de los ataques de asma, así como a mejorar la función pulmonar.

En cuanto a la rinitis alérgica, este medicamento se utiliza para aliviar los síntomas como la congestión nasal, la secreción nasal, la picazón en la nariz y los estornudos causados por alergias estacionales o perennes.

El Dr. Javier López, especialista en medicina familiar y comunitaria, nos explica qué son los principales **medicamentos** antihistamínicos como la Loratadina y para qué sirven. Descubre cómo este medicamento ayuda a tratar los síntomas de la **alergia al polvo** y la **rinitis alergica**. Aprende sobre la **histamina** y cómo la Loratadina actúa en tu **salud** para aliviar las molestias de la **nariz**.

La loratadina es un medicamento antihistamínico utilizado comúnmente para tratar los síntomas de alergias, como estornudos, picazón, ojos llorosos y nariz mocosa. Este fármaco bloquea la acción de la histamina, una sustancia en el cuerpo que causa síntomas de alergia.

### ¿Para qué se usa la loratadina?

1. **Alergias**: Es eficaz en el tratamiento de reacciones alérgicas leves a moderadas, como las causadas por el polen, el polvo, los ácaros del polvo, la caspa de mascotas, entre otros.

2. **Urticaria**: También puede usarse para tratar la urticaria (ronchas rojas y elevadas en la piel que pican), ayudando a aliviar el picor y la hinchazón.

Các Dạng Bào Chế Montelukas
Viên nhai: Montelukast natri 4mg, 5mg.

Viên nén bao phim: Montelukast natri 10mg.

Cốm pha hỗn dịch uống: montelukast natri 4mg.

Công dụng (Chỉ định) MONTELUKAST
MONTELUKAST được chỉ định như liệu pháp điều trị bổ sung ở những bệnh nhân suyễn mận mức độ nhẹ đen trung bình không kiểm soát được bằng corticosteroid dạng hít và những bệnh nhân mà chủ vận 3 tác dụng ngắn “khi cần thiết” không kiểm soát được triệu chứng.
MONTELUKAST cũng được chỉ định trong dự phòng suyễn, trong đó chủ yếu là dự phòng co thắt phế quản cẩp do vạn động thể lực.

Cách dùng - Liều dùng
Trẻ em từ 6 đến 14 tuổi mắc bệnh hen suyễn hay viêm mũi dị ứng theo mùa: 1 viên nhai 5mg/ ngày.

Trẻ em từ 2 đến 5 tuổi mắc bệnh hen suyễn hay viêm mũi dị ứng theo mùa: 1 viên nhai 4mg/ ngày.

Bệnh nhân suyễn từ 15 tuổi trơ lên, hoặc bị suyễn đồng thời bị viêm mũi dị ứng theo mùa là 10 mg hàng ngày, uống vào buổi tối.

Khuyến cáo chung. Hiệu quả điều trị của PMS-MONTELUKAST trên các thông số kiểm soát suyễn đạt được trong vòng một ngày.

PMS-MONTELUKAST có thể được sử dụng cung hoặc không cùng với thức ăn. Bệnh nhân nên tiếp tục dùng PMS-MONTELUKAST ngay cả khi bệnh suyễn của họ được kiểm soátmcũng như khi bệnh suyễn xấu đi. PMS-MONTELUKAST không nên dùng đồng thời với các sản phẩm khác có chứa thành phần hoạt chất tương tự montelukast.

Không cần chỉnh liều ở người cao tuồi, bệnh nhân suy thận hoặc suy gan nhẹ đến trung bình. Không có dữ liệu trên bệnh nhân suy gan nặng. Liều dùng ợ bệnh nhân nam và nữ là như nhau.

title: Pharmacology of Montelukast (Singulair) ; Mechanism of action, Pharmacokinetics, Uses, Effects
description:
Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist that is frequently used in managing asthma, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, and allergic rhinitis2.

Mechanism of Action
Leukotriene Receptor Antagonist: Montelukast works by blocking the action of leukotriene D4 (LTD4) at the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 (CysLT1) in the lungs2. By inhibiting LTD4, it helps to reduce bronchoconstriction, inflammation, and mucus secretion.

Anti-Inflammatory Effect: By blocking leukotrienes, which are inflammatory mediators, montelukast reduces airway inflammation and the associated symptoms of asthma and other allergic conditions.

Pharmacokinetics
Absorption: Rapidly absorbed after oral administration, with bioavailability of 63-73%.

Protein Binding: Approximately 99% of montelukast is bound to plasma proteins.

Metabolism: Primarily metabolized in the liver via the cytochrome P450 enzymes, including CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9.

Half-life: The elimination half-life ranges from 2.7 to 5.5 hours.

Excretion: Excreted mainly via the bile.

Clinical Uses
1. Asthma: Used as a long-term control medication to prevent asthma attacks, and for patients whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by inhaled corticosteroids alone. 22. Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction: Helps to prevent breathing problems during exercise. 32. Allergic Rhinitis: Alleviates symptoms of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, such as nasal congestion, sneezing, and runny nose. 4. Chronic Urticaria: Treats chronic hives of long duration.

Side Effects
Common: Abdominal pain, cough, headache.

Serious: Rarely, it may cause allergic reactions such as anaphylaxis, eosinophilic conditions, neuropsychiatric effects like agitation, hallucinations, depression, and suicidal behavior.

Dosage and Administration
Oral: Usually taken once daily in the evening. The dosage may vary based on age, condition severity, and response to treatment.

title: SINGULAIR (montelukast), singulair para que sirve, singulair 10 mg
description:
¿Qué es Singulair y para qué sirve? 


¿Qué es Singulair? 


Singulair es un antagonista del receptor de leucotrienos que bloquea unas sustancias llamadas leucotrienos. 

 
¿Cómo actúa Singulair? 


Los leucotrienos producen estrechamiento e hinchazón de las vías respiratorias en los pulmones y también pueden causar síntomas de alergia.  Al bloquear los leucotrienos,  Singulair mejora los síntomas del asma,  ayuda a controlar el asma y mejora los síntomas de la alergia estacional (también conocida como fiebre del heno o rinitis alérgica estacional). 

 
¿Cuándo se debe usar Singulair? 


Su médico le ha recetado Singulair para tratar el asma y prevenir los síntomas de su asma durante el día y la noche. 

 
¿Para qué sirve Singulair? 


Singulair se utiliza para el tratamiento de adultos y adolescentes de 15 años de edad y mayores que no están adecuadamente controlados con su medicación y necesitan tratamiento adicional. 
Singulair también ayuda a prevenir el estrechamiento de las vías aéreas provocado por el ejercicio. 
En aquellos pacientes asmáticos en los que Singulair está indicado para el asma,  Singulair también puede proporcionar alivio sintomático de la rinitis alérgica estacional. 

Dependiendo de los síntomas y de la gravedad de su asma,  su médico determinará cómo debe usar Singulair. 



¿Cómo tomar Singulair? 


Siga exactamente las instrucciones de administración de este medicamento indicadas por su médico o farmacéutico.  En caso de duda,  consulte de nuevo a su médico o farmacéutico. 

Sólo debe tomar un comprimido de Singulair una vez al día,  como se lo ha recetado su médico. 
Debe tomarse incluso cuando no tenga síntomas o cuando tenga una crisis de asma aguda. 
 

Para adultos y adolescentes de 15 años de edad y mayores. 

La dosis recomendada es un comprimido de 10 mg diariamente por la noche. 

Si está tomando Singulair,  asegúrese de que no toma ningún otro producto que contenga el mismo principio activo,  montelukast. 

Este medicamento se toma por vía oral. 

Puede tomar Singulair 10 mg con o sin alimentos. 

 
Si toma más Singulair del que debe. 


Pida ayuda a su médico inmediatamente. 

En la mayoría de los casos de sobredosis no se comunicaron efectos adversos.  Los síntomas que se produjeron con más frecuencia comunicados en la sobredosis en adultos y en niños fueron dolor abdominal,  somnolencia,  sed,  dolor de cabeza,  vómitos e hiperactividad. 

Consulte inmediatamente a su médico,  farmacéutico,  indicando el medicamento y la cantidad tomada.  Se recomendará llevar el envase y el prospecto del medicamento al profesional sanitario. 

 

Posibles efectos adversos. 


Al igual que todos los medicamentos,  este medicamento puede producir efectos adversos,  aunque no todas las personas los sufran. 

En ensayos clínicos realizados con Singulair 10 mg comprimidos recubiertos con película,  los efectos adversos relacionados con la administración del medicamento y notificados con más frecuencia fueron:

dolor abdominal. 
dolor de cabeza. 
infección respiratoria alta. 
diarrea,  náuseas,  vómitos. 
erupción cutánea. 
fiebre. 
enzimas del hígado elevadas. 

Si experimenta cualquier tipo de efecto adverso,  consulte a su médico o farmacéutico,  incluso si se trata de posibles efectos adversos que no aparecen en este vídeo.

title: Capsular Contracture
description:
The formation of a "capsule" of scar tissue around any implant (medical or cosmetic) is a normal part of the healing process. The body reacts to any foreign object by creating a barrier of scar tissue around it. This capsule formation is beneficial, especially for breast implants, as it offers protective and aesthetic benefits by keeping the implants in their proper position.

What surgeons and patients seek to avoid is capsular 𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙩𝙧𝙖𝙘𝙩𝙪𝙧𝙚– a condition where the scar tissue becomes unusually hard and starts to contract around the implant, leading to aesthetic problems and, in severe cases, breast pain.

#Singulair (montelukast) is gaining recognition for its off-label potential in reducing or reversing #CapsularContracture. It works by blocking leukotrienes, substances that contribute to inflammation and scar tissue formation. By reducing these inflammatory responses, Singulair may soften the scar tissue around the implant, alleviating pain and improving the breast's appearance.

title: 🧧MONTELUKAST (SINGULAIR 10 mg)✨ Que es y Para Que Sirve ✨Efectos Secundarios✨
description:
Montelukast 10 mg es un medicamento utilizado para tratar diferentes condiciones respiratorias, principalmente el asma y la rinitis alérgica. Pertenece a una clase de fármacos conocidos como antagonistas de los receptores de leucotrienos. Los leucotrienos son sustancias químicas en el cuerpo que desempeñan un papel importante en la inflamación y la respuesta alérgica.

Su principal función es bloquear la acción de los leucotrienos, lo que ayuda a reducir la inflamación en las vías respiratorias, relajar los músculos bronquiales y mejorar los síntomas asociados con el asma y la rinitis alérgica.

En el caso del asma, Montelukast 10 mg se utiliza tanto para el tratamiento crónico como para la prevención de los ataques agudos de asma en adultos y niños mayores de 6 años. Ayuda a reducir la frecuencia y la gravedad de los ataques de asma, así como a mejorar la función pulmonar.

En cuanto a la rinitis alérgica, este medicamento se utiliza para aliviar los síntomas como la congestión nasal, la secreción nasal, la picazón en la nariz y los estornudos causados por alergias estacionales o perennes.

Como cualquier medicamento, Montelukast 10 mg puede tener efectos secundarios. Algunos de los efectos secundarios más comunes incluyen dolor de cabeza, dolor abdominal, fatiga, fiebre, tos, dolor de garganta y náuseas. En casos raros, puede causar efectos secundarios más graves como reacciones alérgicas graves, cambios de humor, depresión, e incluso pensamientos o intentos de suicidio, aunque estos son extremadamente raros.

Montelukast 10 mg se comercializa bajo diferentes nombres de marca en diferentes países. Uno de los nombres comerciales más comunes es Singulair, pero también puede encontrarse bajo otras marcas dependiendo del fabricante y la región geográfica.

Es importante tener en cuenta que Montelukast 10 mg debe ser utilizado bajo la supervisión y prescripción de un médico, ya que solo un profesional de la salud puede determinar si es el tratamiento adecuado para cada persona, así como supervisar cualquier efecto secundario que pueda surgir durante su uso.

description:
Costuma utilizar alguma dessa medicações no nariz?

Muitas pessoas confundem os corticoides nasais (noex, busonid, avamys, nasonex...) e os vasoconstritores nasais (neosoro, afrin, freenal, narix...).

Os corticoides nasais são excelentes medicações usadas no controle das rinite alérgicas e rinossinusites. Já os vasoconstritores nasais são medicações utilizada para o alívio imediato da obstrução nasal.

O problemas é que muitas pessoas utilizam esses vasoconstritores nasais há meses ou anos. 

Como consequência, elas apresentarão os efeitos colaterias deles que são:
Rinite medicamentosa (o nariz vai continuar obstruído)
Sangramentos nasais
Dores de cabeça

title: Cuidado com medicamentos usados para aliviar sintomas da rinite
description:
Spray ou gotas para rinite: qual a diferença e quando usar?

Se você sofre com rinite alérgica, provavelmente já usou algum medicamento intranasal, seja em spray ou gotas. Mas você sabe para que serve cada um e quais devem ser evitados? Vamos esclarecer:

✔ Soro fisiológico: essencial para a higiene nasal, ajuda a remover alérgenos e secreções, melhorando a respiração sem causar efeitos colaterais. Pode ser usado diariamente.

⚠ Descongestionantes tópicos: apesar de aliviarem rapidamente a obstrução nasal, não tratam a causa da rinite e podem causar efeito rebote, piorando a congestão quando usados por mais de 3 a 5 dias. O uso prolongado pode levar à rinite medicamentosa, tornando o nariz dependente do medicamento para respirar.
Exemplo: nafazolina, oximetazolina

✔ Corticoides nasais: são os mais indicados para rinite alérgica, pois reduzem a inflamação e os sintomas de forma segura e eficaz. Devem ser usados sob orientação médica para garantir a dose e o tempo corretos.
Exemplos: budesonida, beclometasona, mometasona, fluticasona. 

⚠ Cuidado com a automedicação! Usar o medicamento errado pode piorar os sintomas e trazer riscos à saúde. Sempre consulte um especialista para encontrar o melhor tratamento para o seu caso!

description:
Day 7 of switching from Dupixent (Dupilumab) + Rinvoq (upadacitinib) to Dupixent + Cibinqo (abrocitinib). 

Observations: Skin has cleared up a lot by Day 4. Skin feels better now on Dupixent + Cinbinqo than when I was on Dupixent + Rinvoq.

Cibinqo (abrocitinib) is an oral, once-daily [Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor] approved for treating moderate-to-severe [atopic dermatitis (eczema)] in adults and adolescents aged 12+ [who haven't responded to other treatments]. It works primarily by inhibiting [JAK1], reducing inflammation and [itching]. Key [side effects include nausea, headache, acne, and herpes simplex].

Rinvoq (upadacitinib) is a once-daily, oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that treats chronic inflammatory diseases by blocking signals that cause overactive immune responses. It is FDA-approved for conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, atopic dermatitis, psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease, ankylosing spondylitis, and giant cell arteritis.

title: Dermatite atópica grave: Como controlar? #dermatiteatopica #alergia #dermatite #eczema #dupixent
description:
Fiquei muito feliz com esse caso e vou explicar o porquê.

O paciente que aparece no vídeo chegou ao consultório com essas lesões e tem dermatite atópica grave. Ele já havia feito vários tratamentos que traziam apenas melhora temporária. Sempre que usava corticoide oral ou injeções de depósito como o Diprospan, a pele melhorava por alguns dias, mas logo depois tudo voltava novamente.

Isso acontece porque, em muitos casos de dermatite atópica, a pele lesionada pode ficar colonizada por bactérias, fungos ou vírus. Nesse caso , as lesões estavam colonizadas principalmente por bactérias, principalmente Staphylococcus aureus, algo muito comum quando a pele está machucada e inflamada. 
Essas infecções secundárias pioram muito a inflamação e fazem a doença parecer fora de controle.

Por isso, o primeiro passo é tratar a infecção, muitas vezes com antibiótico por alguns dias. Só isso já pode trazer uma melhora importante das lesões.

Mas o que me deixou muito feliz nesse caso é que ele tem plano de saúde, e isso facilita muito o acesso aos tratamentos mais modernos para dermatite atópica grave.

Hoje existem opções eficazes como:

💊 Imunossupressores como ciclosporina e metotrexato
💊 Inibidores de JAK: Rinvoq
💉 Imunobiológicos como o Dupixent

No caso desse paciente, vamos iniciar ciclosporina. Se ele responder bem, ótimo. Se não houver melhora adequada ou surgirem efeitos colaterais, existe a possibilidade de iniciar o Dupixent, que costuma ser coberto pelo plano de saúde em casos graves como o dele.

Ou seja, com o tratamento adequado, a chance de melhora nos próximos meses é muito grande e o paciente pode recuperar qualidade de vida.

title: POV: You’re Done With Eczema Creams
description:
Sources- PMID 37552431 
sitraub on TT 

For individuals living with severe eczema or asthma, the traditional treatment cycle can feel like an endless treadmill of topical steroids, oral immunosuppressants, or rescue inhalers that only offer temporary relief. When these conventional methods fail, it is often because the underlying cause is Type 2 (T2) inflammation, a specific overactive immune response driven by proteins called interleukin-4 (IL-4) and interleukin-13 (IL-13). Dupilumab (brand name Dupixent) has emerged as a biological "lifeline" by acting as a targeted antibody that blocks the shared receptor for these two proteins. Unlike broad immunosuppressants that dampen the entire immune system—often leading to significant side effects—dupilumab precisely "plugs" the cellular lock that these inflammatory keys use to trigger symptoms, effectively silencing the storm at its source without leaving the rest of the body vulnerable. The real-world impact of this targeted approach is often life-changing for those who have "maxed out" other options. In clinical studies, many asthma patients were able to significantly reduce or even eliminate their dependence on oral corticosteroids, which are notorious for long-term risks like bone loss and weight gain. For eczema sufferers, the drug can lead to a dramatic reduction in the "unbearable itch" and visible skin lesions, often achieving clear or almost-clear skin within months. By addressing the molecular root of the inflammation rather than just masking the symptoms, dupilumab allows the skin barrier to heal and the airways to stay open, offering a path to normalcy for patients whose lives were previously dictated by the severity of their condition.

description:
ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is a specialized IVF procedure where a single healthy sperm is carefully selected and injected directly into a mature egg using a microscopic needle 🔬🧬

This technique helps improve fertilization in cases of male factor infertility such as low sperm count, poor sperm motility, previous fertilization failure, and other fertility challenges.

Every movement during the procedure requires extreme precision, stability, and care because even the tiniest step can play a huge role in the journey toward creating life 🤍✨

title: Serena Williams Told Michelle Obama What It's Like to Win a Grand Slam Pregnant! 🎾🏆🥹
description:
Two of the most powerful women in the world sat down together — and got more honest than anyone expected.
In a special live episode of Michelle Obama's IMO podcast on May 13, tennis legend Serena Williams joined her longtime friend to talk about motherhood, fertility, and raising daughters. The conversation hit differently.
Michelle went first. "I don't know about all of you, but I know that when I struggled to conceive, I took that on like a personal failure," Obama told the gathered crowd. The former First Lady — who eventually conceived daughters Sasha and Malia through IVF — spoke openly about the silent shame that comes with infertility, especially for Black women. According to a 2025 study by the National Women's Law Center, Black women are almost twice as likely as Hispanic or non-Hispanic white women to experience infertility in the United States.
Then Serena added her voice: "I don't think we have that conversation enough about how many times you conceive and have a miscarriage, or whether you conceive and it doesn't work."
And then came the moment that stopped the room. Serena shared what it was like to win a Grand Slam while pregnant — famously taking the 2017 Australian Open title without yet knowing she was eight weeks along. She also opened up about her mother's role as her greatest coach — recalling how, ranked 89th in the world with everyone writing her off, her mom told her exactly how to beat Maria Sharapova in the final. "She told me, 'You got this.' And she told me exactly how to play. And I won in less than an hour. It was really genius."
Two icons. One honest conversation. And a room full of people realizing they weren't alone. 🥹

title: Fertility Treatment After Losing a Child | An Emotional Journey of Hope, IVF & Motherhood
description:
Fertility Treatment After Losing a Child | An Emotional Journey of Hope, IVF & Motherhood
.
.
Fertility treatment is not just about medicines, injections, scans, or IVF. It is an emotional roller coaster where doctors also deeply feel the pain, hope, and dreams of every couple.

In this emotional real-life experience, a couple came to me after losing their 19-20 year old son in a tragic accident. They were unable to even speak. Tears were flowing, and they simply showed me their son’s photo on their mobile phone.

The mother was above 40 years of age, and medically the chances looked very low. We discussed the possibility of IVF and even ovum donor treatment. But when we evaluated her ovarian reserve and antral follicle count, there was still a small ray of hope. Her periods were regular, ovulation induction was started… and by God’s grace, she conceived naturally.

She delivered a healthy baby boy at full term.
The parents told me:
“Doctor, you gave our child back to us.”

Moments like these remind us that fertility treatment is not only science. Sometimes faith, hope, emotions, and the blessings of the Almighty also play a role.

Today, fertility treatment has become a boon for couples struggling with infertility, advanced maternal age, low ovarian reserve, or emotional loss. Every couple deserves the chance to build a family because becoming parents is one of the deepest emotional needs of human life.

If your biological clock is running, do not delay fertility evaluation and treatment. Early diagnosis and timely treatment can make a huge difference.

Because behind every fertility journey… there is a story, a pain, and a hope waiting to become a family.

Dr. Seema Agarwal
Obstetrician & Gynecologist | Fertility Specialist

Human beings build civilizations, then spend centuries pretending emotions are irrational while entire lives revolve around one small word: family. Biology really said, “Here, have hormones and heartbreak together.” Brutal design, honestly.

💉 Why do fertility doctors recommend Donor Sperm in IVF?

Here are the main reasons:

✅ Zero sperm count (Azoospermia) or very low sperm count  
✅ Poor sperm quality that doesn’t improve with treatment  
✅ Genetic or hereditary diseases in the male partner  
✅ Previous multiple failed IVF cycles with husband’s sperm  
✅ Single women or same-sex female couples wanting to conceive  

Donor sperm is carefully screened, tested and used in IUI or IVF-ICSI. Many couples have successfully become parents through this option ❤️

It’s a personal choice and completely confidential in most clinics.

Fertility doesn’t wait for the “perfect time.” ⏳

As age increases:
• Ovarian reserve declines
• Egg quality reduces
• AMH levels may drop
• IVF success rates can decrease

Many couples spend years trying naturally, exploring home remedies, supplements, or delaying treatment… only to start IVF when fertility chances are already lower.

The truth?
IVF often gives better results when started at the RIGHT time — not the last moment.

Early fertility assessment can help you understand:
✔ Egg count & ovarian reserve
✔ Fertility potential
✔ Chances of natural conception
✔ When IVF may actually help

Your biological clock is real — and timely decisions can make all the difference. ❤️

Don’t delay decisions that depend on biology.

description:
A new report from the CDC's National Center for Health Statistics has confirmed a historic first in American demographics. For the first time ever in recorded US history births to women over 40 have surpassed births to teenagers. Women over 30 now account for more than half of all American births  up from just 30% in 1990. Experts attribute the shift to women prioritizing education careers and financial security before starting families along with major advances in fertility treatments including IVF and egg freezing that have made later pregnancies safer and more accessible than ever before. Read this if you’re trying to conceive with Low AMH.
And first of all — don’t panic ❤️‍🩹

I know how draining it feels when you’ve been trying for months or years… and suddenly your reports show the words “Low AMH.”
Most women immediately start believing that natural pregnancy is no longer possible —
but that’s NOT always true ✨

What many people don’t understand is this:
AMH mainly tells you about egg quantity, not egg quality.
And for pregnancy… your body doesn’t need “many” eggs.
It needs healthy ovulation and even ONE good-quality egg can be enough to conceive 👶💕

That’s why stressing over AMH numbers only harms your hormones more.
Stress affects ovulation, fertility, sleep — everything 😣💭

Instead, shift your focus towards supporting your body naturally:

✨ Improving blood flow to the ovaries
✨ Supporting hormonal balance
✨ Reducing stress on the nervous system
✨ Improving sleep, nutrition & daily lifestyle

And this is exactly where yoga, pranayama, and meditation create powerful changes 🌿🧘‍♀️
I’ve seen so many women with Low AMH conceive naturally once they stopped chasing reports and started supporting their body with patience.

Your body is not asking for fear right now…

title: The 4 Phase of Menstrual Cycle #fertility #acupuncture #fertilitysupport #shorts #viralvideo
description:
Every phase of your cycle has a different hormonal landscape and what supports you in one phase isn’t what supports you in another. Generic advice misses this completely.

These are the 4 phases and why a one-size-fits-all plan will always fall short:

1. Menstrual phase — hormones are at their lowest. Your body needs rest, warmth, and replenishment.

2. Follicular phase — estrogen rises as your body prepares an egg. Energy builds, and so does your capacity for movement and nourishment that supports egg quality.

3. Ovulation — estrogen peaks and LH surges to release the egg. This is your fertile window. Circulation and stress regulation matter most here.

4. Luteal phase — progesterone takes over to prepare the uterine lining. Your body needs grounding, steady blood sugar, and support for implantation.

In my practice at Mighty River Wellness Clinic in Los Angeles, we map fertility care to where you actually are in your cycle. Natural conception, IVF, embryo transfer...the strategy shifts because your body shifts.

title: 🧐 Comment savoir si une contraception est fiable ?
description:
Pour établir le taux de fiabilité d’une méthode de contraception, on se base sur l’indice de Pearl, qui donne le nombre de grossesses non désirées pendant un an, sur 100 couples ayant utilisé la méthode en question. 

À partir de là, on retrouve : 

- L’indice de Pearl théorique (ou taux de fiabilité théorique), établi lorsque la méthode est parfaitement employée, dans des conditions de laboratoire
- L’indice de Pearl pratique (ou taux de fiabilité pratique), établi lorsque la méthode est utilisée par des couples “dans la vraie vie”, en tenant compte des aléas du quotidien, des oublis etc.

Par exemple, le taux de fiabilité théorique de la pilule est de 99,7%, mais son taux de fiabilité pratique est de 97%. Pour la symptothermie, on est sur 99,6% d’efficacité théorique et 98,2% en pratique.
